- On PostgreSQL write `? |` with a space for a bind followed by OR; `?|` and `?&`
  are operators. On PostgreSQL a fragment may use native `$n` placeholders instead
  (see "Porting pgx and sqlc SQL" below); do not mix them with `?`/`@name`.
- Returned results of raw queries bypass soft-delete, hooks and timestamps.

#### Porting pgx and sqlc SQL

On the PostgreSQL dialect, raw SQL (`Exec`, `Scalars`, `SQL`, `TypedSQL`,
`RawSubquery`) accepts PostgreSQL's native `$1, $2, ...` placeholders, so a
statement written for pgx or sqlc moves over unchanged:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// pgx / sqlc:   pool.Exec(ctx, "UPDATE tasks SET done = $1 WHERE owner = $2 OR creator = $2", true, uid)
affected, err := momo.Exec(ctx, q, "UPDATE tasks SET done = $1 WHERE owner = $2 OR creator = $2", true, uid)
```

Rules:

- `$n` binds positional argument n of that call. A reused `$n` (here `$2`) binds
  the argument once. An `In`, `Ident` or `Expr` argument is rendered again at each
  use. Momo renumbers: inside a larger statement (`TypedSQL` or `RawSubquery`
  after earlier `Where` binds) `$1` still means the fragment's first argument.
- One style per fragment. Mixing `$n` with `?`, `@name` or `Named` is
  `ErrValidation`.
- Every `$n` needs an argument (`$3` with two arguments, or `$0`, is
  `ErrValidation`) and every argument must be used (a gap such as `$1, $3` is
  `ErrValidation`), so a typo fails at build time.
- A `$n` inside a string literal, quoted identifier, comment or dollar-quoted body
  is text, not a placeholder.
- Other dialects: `$n` is `ErrUnsupported` at build time on SQLite and MySQL,
  even when the fragment has no `?`. Port such statements to `?` (or `@name`)
  when the code must run on SQLite or MySQL.
- A literal `$n` that must reach the server as text, as in `PREPARE` or a
  `CREATE FUNCTION` body that refers to its parameters, is read as a placeholder
  and fails with `ErrValidation` for a missing argument. Put it where momo
  treats it as text: inside a string literal or a dollar-quoted body, for example
  `DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'PREPARE p AS SELECT $1::int'; END $$`.
- Behaviour change: before native `$n` support a `$1` in raw PostgreSQL SQL went
  to the server untouched. It is now a momo placeholder, so a statement that used
  `$1` as text needs the treatment above.
- sqlc `sqlc.arg(name)` / `@name` styles: use `momo.Named("name", v)` with `@name`.
- Typed casts keep working: `$1::int` is fine.

`SelectQuery.SQL()` returns `Compiled{SQL, Args}` without running. `Explain(ctx)`
runs `EXPLAIN` (never `ANALYZE`) and returns plan text; it binds parameters and
does not execute the query. Inside a `Tx`, it sees that transaction's settings.

Select-time guards: `Limit`/`Offset` negative is `ErrValidation`.

Details: README sections 5-7, [capabilities.md](capabilities.md).
Examples: [crud-zero-null](../examples/crud-zero-null/),
[projection-pagination](../examples/projection-pagination/).

## 7. Transactions

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
err := db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
	// use tx (a momo.Querier), NOT db, for everything in here
	if _, err := momo.Update[models.Account](tx).
		Set(account.Balance.SetExpr(momo.TypedSQL[int64]("balance + ?", amt))).
		Where(account.Owner.Eq(to)).Exec(ctx); err != nil {
		return err // any error (or panic) rolls back
	}
	return nil // nil commits
})
```

- `db.Tx(ctx, opts, fn)` commits on nil, rolls back on error or panic. `fn` runs
  exactly once; Momo never retries it.
- DON'T use `db` inside the closure: it runs outside the transaction on another
  connection and can deadlock on a small pool.
- `TxOptions{ReadOnly: true}` makes the server refuse writes (SQLSTATE 25006;
  Momo has no sentinel for it: `errors.As(err, &pgErr)` with
  `*pgconn.PgError`). `TxOptions{Isolation: sql.LevelSerializable}` sets the level;
  supported: read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, serializable. Any
  other level is `ErrUnsupported`.
- Savepoints: `tx.Tx(ctx, func(sp *momo.Tx) error {...})` runs in a savepoint; if
  it fails only its work is undone and the outer transaction continues. Without a
  savepoint PostgreSQL aborts the whole transaction at the first error. Manual:
  `tx.Savepoint(ctx, name)`, `tx.RollbackTo(ctx, name)`, `tx.Release(ctx, name)`.
- Manual control: `tx, err := db.Begin(ctx, opts)`, `tx.Commit(ctx)`,
  `tx.Rollback(ctx)`; a finished `*Tx` returns `ErrTxDone`. Prefer `db.Tx`.
- Incremental adoption in a `database/sql` or pgx codebase, both directions:
  - Adopt a transaction the caller began: `mtx := db.AdoptTx(pgxdriver.SQLTx(sqlTx))`
    for a `*sql.Tx` (database must be pgx-stdlib backed, `FromSQLDB`), or
    `db.AdoptTx(pgxdriver.PgxTx(pgxTx, opts...))` for a `pgx.Tx` (pgxpool driver; `opts` are the options of `New`, such as `WithExecMode`; an unsupported exec mode returns `ErrUnsupported` on use, as with `New`). An adopted `pgx.Tx` keeps Batch and `COPY`; an adopted `*sql.Tx` has neither. Statements,
    hooks, error classification and savepoints (`mtx.Tx`) work as usual. `Commit`
    and `Rollback` on `mtx` return `ErrAdoptedTx` and do nothing: the caller
    commits or rolls back its own transaction. After that, `mtx` statements
    return `ErrTxDone`. A nil argument panics.
  - Expose the handle behind a `*Tx` to legacy helpers:
    `pgxdriver.UnwrapSQLTx(tx)` returns `(*sql.Tx, bool)` and
    `pgxdriver.UnwrapPgxTx(tx)` returns `(pgx.Tx, bool)`; `false` when the `Tx`
    belongs to the other driver kind. Works for `db.Tx` callbacks, adopted
    transactions and savepoint scopes (the outer transaction). Finish a
    momo-begun transaction through momo, never through the unwrapped handle.
  - Mixing is safe: a legacy `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` helper and momo statements
    can alternate on the same transaction.
- Do not call blocking network I/O inside `fn`.
- Retry the WHOLE `db.Tx` on `ErrSerialization` (PostgreSQL 40001 serialization
  failure and 40P01 deadlock). Only when `fn` has no side effects outside the
  database. Copy of `examples/transactions`:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
func retrySerializable(ctx context.Context, db *momo.DB, fn func(tx *momo.Tx) error) error {
	const (
		maxAttempts = 3
		backoff     = 20 * time.Millisecond // doubles in a real service
	)
	var err error
	for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++ {
		err = db.Tx(ctx, momo.TxOptions{Isolation: sql.LevelSerializable}, fn)
		if !errors.Is(err, momo.ErrSerialization) {
			return err
		}
		if attempt == maxAttempts {
			break // out of attempts: return the error without sleeping
		}
		d := backoff/2 + rand.N(backoff) // math/rand/v2: jitter so competitors do not collide in lockstep
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return ctx.Err()
		case <-time.After(d):
		}
	}
	return err
}
```

- On a pinned connection (`db.OnConn(pc)`) transactions are not available:
  `Begin`, `Tx`, `Replace`, `CreateGraph` return `ErrUnsupported`.
- Several momo helpers open their own transaction on a `*DB` and a savepoint on a
  `*Tx`: `Replace`, `CreateGraph`, chunked `Insert.Models`, `WithSearch`.

Details: README section 8. Example: [transactions](../examples/transactions/).

## 8. Relations

Declare with tags (section 4). Relations never load by themselves: a plain
`Select` leaves relation fields empty. Relation descriptors (`document.Comments`)
are immutable and concurrency-safe.

Decision table:

| Need                                                        | API                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Children for rows you already fetched                       | `momo.Load(ctx, q, parents, rel, opts...)`: one statement per relation, not per parent                                                                                                                                 |
| Several relations for the same parents                      | `momo.LoadAll(ctx, q, parents, rel1, rel2.Scope(opts...), rel3.Then(nested...))`                                                                                                                                       |
| Filter, order and nest one relation                         | `rel.Scope(where, orderBy).Then(nested)` with `LoadWhere` and `LoadOrderBy` options                                                                                                                                    |
| Load as part of a query (`All`/`One`/`First`)               | a select query's `.Preload(rel, ...)`                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Belongs-to with no extra round trip                         | `Preload(rel.Joined())`: LEFT JOIN in the parent statement                                                                                                                                                             |
| Only some children, ordered, top-N per parent, soft-deleted | `rel.Scope(opts...)` with `LoadWhere`, `LoadOrderBy`, `LoadPerParentLimit`, `LoadWithDeleted`, `LoadOnlyDeleted` (each generic over the child type, as in the example below; `Load` accepts the same options directly) |
| Children of children                                        | `rel.Then(nested...)`                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Filter parents by children                                  | `Where(rel.Has(scope...))`, `rel.HasNo(...)`, `rel.HasFrom(parentAlias, ...)`                                                                                                                                          |
| Order parents by child count                                | `OrderBy(rel.CountOrder(momo.DirDesc))`                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Children matching a parent query, no parent fetched         | `rel.From(parentQuery)` returns `SelectQuery[C]` (not many-to-many)                                                                                                                                                    |
| Add or remove links to EXISTING rows                        | `rel.Link(ctx, q, &parent, &c1, &c2)`, `rel.Unlink(...)`, `rel.Count(ctx, q, &parent)`                                                                                                                                 |
| Make the linked set exactly this one                        | `rel.Replace(ctx, q, &parent, children...)`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Insert a parent and NEW children together                   | `momo.CreateGraph(ctx, q, &parent, rel1.Include(), rel2.Include())`                                                                                                                                                    |
| Get-or-insert on a unique key                               | `momo.FindOrCreate(ctx, q, []momo.ColumnRef{author.Name}, &a)` returns `(created bool, err)`                                                                                                                           |
| Insert or update by primary key                             | `momo.UpsertByPK(ctx, q, &m)`                                                                                                                                                                                          |

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
docs, err := momo.Select[models.Document](db).
	Preload(
		document.Author.Joined(),
		document.Comments.Scope(
			momo.LoadWhere[models.Comment](comment.Approved.Eq(true)),
			momo.LoadOrderBy[models.Comment](comment.ID.Desc()),
			momo.LoadPerParentLimit[models.Comment](3)),
	).
	Limit(20).All(ctx)

withApproved := momo.Select[models.Document](db).
	Where(document.Comments.Has(comment.Approved.As("momo_r").Eq(true))) // child alias is momo_r

err = document.Tags.Link(ctx, db, &doc, &models.Tag{ID: 1}, &models.Tag{ID: 2})

doc := models.Document{Title: "Hello", Author: &models.Author{Name: "Ada"},
	Comments: []models.Comment{{Body: "first"}}}
err = momo.CreateGraph(ctx, db, &doc, document.Author.Include(), document.Comments.Include())
```

Rules and limits:

- `Load`/`LoadAll`/`Preload` clear the association first, so a parent with no
  children is empty (nil), never stale. NULL-key parents get an empty
  association. Parent order never changes.
- `Scope(...)` and `Then(...)` combine: both return a `RelationLoader` with
  `Scope` and `Then` methods, so
  `document.Comments.Scope(approvedOnly).Then(comment.Author)` (with
  `approvedOnly` a `momo.LoadWhere[models.Comment]` option) filters the comments
  and loads each one's author in one loader. The options
  apply to that relation's children only; nested loaders carry their own; the
  nested level runs over the surviving children only (one statement per level).
- `Joined()` is belongs-to only, and only when the child key is the child's
  primary key or a single unique column. Has-one, has-many, many-to-many give
  `ErrUnsupported`. `momo.Load(ctx, db, docs, X.Joined())` does not compile
  (`Joined()` returns a `Loader`, `Load` wants a `Relation`; cannot infer `C`),
  and `LoadAll` returns `ErrUnsupported`. Also `ErrUnsupported` with `Scope`,
  `Then`, `GroupBy`, `Having`, `ForUpdate`, `Each`, `Iter`. With `Columns` the
  select list must have one expression per mapped field (`ErrValidation`).
  Qualify raw column names in the parent's `Where` (ambiguity with the joined
  table).
- `LoadPerParentLimit(n)`: has-many and many-to-many only (belongs-to and has-one
  `ErrUnsupported`); `n < 0` is `ErrValidation`; 0 is unlimited. `LoadWhere`
  filters before the limit.
- `Has`/`HasNo` predicates must name the child column through the alias
  `momo_r`: `comment.Approved.As("momo_r").Eq(true)`; an unaliased column refers
  to the OUTER table.
- Has-one that matches several children for a parent: `ErrTooManyRows`.
- `Link`, `Unlink`, `Replace`, `Count` write SQL directly: model hooks, field
  hooks and `UpdatedAt` are NOT run. Use the model's update path when those must
  run. They never modify the values you pass.
- Many-to-many `Link` relies on a primary or unique key over the join columns.
  Join tables generated from `many2many` tags have one. A hand-written join table
  needs a unique key, or `Link` inserts duplicates.
- Has-one/has-many `Unlink` and `Replace` clear the foreign key: it must be
  nullable, else `ErrNotNullViolation`. Delete the children instead if they cannot
  exist without a parent.
- Belongs-to is not linkable: all four helpers return `ErrUnsupported`. Set the
  foreign key field on the parent and `Update` it.
- NULL parent key (or NULL child key on many-to-many) is `ErrValidation` for
  `Link`/`Unlink`/`Replace`; `Count` returns 0. `Link`/`Unlink` with no children
  are no-ops.
- `Replace` is a transaction (`*DB`) or savepoint (`*Tx`) and locks the parent row
  (`FOR UPDATE`), so concurrent `Replace` on one parent serialize. `Link`/`Unlink`
  take no lock and may interleave. On a `*Tx` the lock lasts until your
  transaction ends. A non-existent parent locks nothing.
- `Link`/`Unlink` needing several chunks are atomic on a `*DB` (one
  transaction); on a `*Tx` a later chunk failing leaves earlier chunks applied
  until you roll back.
- `CreateGraph`: one level deep; always INSERTs (never matches existing rows);
  belongs-to children first, has-one/has-many after the parent, many-to-many
  children inserted then linked; hooks, timestamps and defaults run. On a `*Tx` it
  runs in a savepoint. Nil parent, a model as its own child, or a NULL key that
  must be copied: `ErrValidation`. Has-many and many-to-many children go in as
  chunked bulk inserts (1000 children = one statement). A dialect without
  `RETURNING` gives `ErrUnsupported` before a transaction opens. DON'T list a
  many-to-many relation whose children are already stored: they are inserted
  again and fail with `ErrUniqueViolation`; use `Link` for existing rows.
- `FindOrCreate` needs a UNIQUE constraint on exactly the key columns. It
  overwrites your struct with the stored row when it exists; a soft-deleted
  row is not found, it fails with `ErrUniqueViolation`. Under REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE the re-select can return
  `ErrNotFound`: retry the transaction. Empty key or unmapped column:
  `ErrValidation`.
- Tag-declared relations: `belongs_to` needs a single-column primary key on its target (the referencing model may have a composite key containing the fk column); `has_one`/`has_many` need one on the parent; `many2many` on both.
- A pipelined load buffers a whole level's child rows (about twice the memory of
  sequential). An unscoped load of a huge has-many is expensive: scope it.
- Many-to-many to self and join tables with extra columns are not supported by tag;
  use an explicit join model struct for extra columns.
- Parent keys are chunked under the bind limit automatically; `WithMaxParams(n)`
  lowers it for tests.

Details: [relations.md](relations.md). Example: [relations](../examples/relations/).

## 9. Vectors

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Item struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:items"`
	ID         int64         `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Title      string        `momo:"size:200"`
	Category   string        `momo:"size:50,index"`
	Embedding  vector.Vector `momo:"dim:1536"` // dim = your embedding model's output size
}

func (i *Item) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
	c.Index("items_embedding_hnsw", &i.Embedding).
		Method("hnsw").
		Opclass(&i.Embedding, "vector_cosine_ops"). // hnsw has NO default opclass: always set it
		With("m", "16").With("ef_construction", "64")
}
```

Column types (the Go type picks the SQL type; `dim` is required for sparsevec and bit,
optional for vector and halfvec):

| Go type               | SQL            | Distance builders                                                     |
| --------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vector.Vector`       | `vector(n)`    | `L2Distance`, `InnerProductDistance`, `CosineDistance`, `L1Distance`  |
| `vector.HalfVector`   | `halfvec(n)`   | same four                                                             |
| `vector.SparseVector` | `sparsevec(n)` | same four (`Dim`, zero-based strictly increasing `Indices`, `Values`) |
| `vector.Bits`         | `bit(n)`       | `HammingDistance`, `JaccardDistance`                                  |

A pointer field (`*vector.Vector`) is nullable (`momo.NullVectorColumn`).
Validation (before the database): length must equal `dim`; NaN and Inf rejected;
halfvec within 65504; max dim 16000 (`vector.MaxDim`). Failures wrap
`ErrValidation` (dimension mismatch, at `SQL()` or first execution) or
`vector.ErrInvalidVector` / `momo.ErrInvalidVector`.

Index rules (`MomoConfig`; validated by the generator, error wraps
`schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex`):

| Method    | Types                           | Max dim for index                    | Opclass `<type>_<x>_ops`, x in                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `hnsw`    | vector, halfvec, sparsevec, bit | vector 2000, halfvec 4000, bit 64000 | `l2`, `ip`, `cosine`, `l1`; bit: `hamming`, `jaccard` |
| `ivfflat` | vector, halfvec, bit            | vector 2000, halfvec 4000, bit 64000 | `l2`, `ip`, `cosine`; bit: `hamming`                  |

- A `vector` column above 2000 dims cannot have an ANN index; store it as
  `HalfVector` (up to 4000 for an index).
- Dimensionless columns: a `vector.Vector` or `vector.HalfVector` field without
  `dim` maps to bare `vector` or `halfvec` and holds embeddings of any size
  (NovaCRM `KbChunk.embedding`). Its descriptor has `Dim()` zero, so a distance
  argument of any size is accepted and still checked for NaN and Inf. Store a
  `dims` column and always filter on it before ordering by distance, since
  pgvector errors when it compares two sizes. hnsw and ivfflat on such a column
  are refused (error wraps `schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex`, names the column), as
  are expression parts; it is searched by sequential scan.
- `hnsw` params: `m` 2..100 (16), `ef_construction` 4..1000 (64, at least 2*m).
  `ivfflat` REQUIRES `With("lists", "N")` (1..32768).
- An index covers one plain column; expression parts are rejected.
- Index opclass must match the distance function: `vector_cosine_ops` with
  `CosineDistance`, `vector_l2_ops` with `L2Distance`, `vector_ip_ops` with
  `InnerProductDistance`, `vector_l1_ops` with `L1Distance`. A mismatch silently
  runs a sequential scan.

Nearest-neighbour query; `Asc()` is nearest first:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
distance := momo.CosineDistance(item.Embedding, query) // query is vector.Vector of dim 1536
hits, err := momo.Select[models.Hit](q). // projection with Title string, Distance float64 (section 4); soft-deleted items are filtered automatically
	From(item.Table).
	Columns(item.Title, distance).
	Where(item.Category.Eq("news")).
	OrderBy(distance.Asc()). // distance only: see the tie-break note below
	Limit(10).
	All(ctx)

// Rows only (the soft-delete filter applies automatically):
items, err := momo.Select[models.Item](q).
	OrderBy(momo.CosineDistance(item.Embedding, query).Asc()).Limit(5).All(ctx)
```

- `Hit` is a projection (section 4); the generator emits its meta. The select
  list is positional, so the field name `Distance` only labels the computed
  column.
- A vector literal is `vector.Vector{0.1, 0.2, 0.3}` (`vector.Vector` is
  `[]float32`; its length must equal `dim`).
- `InnerProductDistance` is pgvector `<#>`: the NEGATIVE inner product, so
  ascending order is closest.
- Vector columns have no `Lt/Le/Gt/Ge/Between`; use a distance builder.
- Passing a dense vector to a bit builder (or the reverse) does not compile.
- `Where` only narrows candidates; it never reorders.
- Order a vector search by the distance alone. Adding a tie-break key such as
  `item.ID.Asc()` makes PostgreSQL sort on top of the index scan, and on some
  versions (seen on PostgreSQL 16) the planner then skips the HNSW or IVFFlat
  index entirely. Order among equal distances is unspecified. Check the plan
  with `Explain` (see [vector-search](../examples/vector-search/)).

Search settings (transaction-scoped; revert at commit or rollback; safe behind
PgBouncer):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
err := db.WithSearch(ctx, momo.SearchSettings{
	HNSWEfSearch:          100,                        // 1..1000 (default 40; at least your LIMIT)
	HNSWIterativeScan:     momo.IterativeRelaxedOrder, // pgvector >= 0.8: filtered searches
	HNSWMaxScanTuples:     20000,                      // pgvector >= 0.8
	HNSWScanMemMultiplier: 2,                          // pgvector >= 0.8; 1..1000 x work_mem
}, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
	// run EVERY vector query for this search on tx, not db
	_, err := momo.Select[models.Item](tx).
		OrderBy(momo.CosineDistance(item.Embedding, query).Asc()).Limit(10).All(ctx)
	return err
})
// Inside an existing transaction: tx.SetSearch(ctx, settings)
```

Fields: `ExactSearch` (turns off index AND bitmap scans for the whole transaction:
exact results, but every other index lookup in that transaction also goes
sequential, so keep it short and dedicated), `HNSWEfSearch`,
`HNSWIterativeScan` (`IterativeOff`, `IterativeRelaxedOrder`,
`IterativeStrictOrder`), `HNSWMaxScanTuples`, `HNSWScanMemMultiplier` (float, 1..1000), `IVFFlatProbes`,
`IVFFlatIterativeScan` (`IterativeOff`, `IterativeRelaxedOrder` only),
`IVFFlatMaxProbes`. Zero leaves the server default. Out of range:
`ErrValidation`. Iterative/max-scan/scan-mem/max-probes fields on pgvector older than 0.8.0
or a missing extension: `ErrUnsupported`.

Pitfalls:

- JSON extraction in GROUP BY: a key that is not plain letters, digits and
  underscores is a bound parameter, and PostgreSQL treats the parameter in the
  select list and the one in GROUP BY as different expressions and rejects the
  query. Plain keys are inlined and group fine, except on a sensitive column,
  whose keys are always bound so they stay masked; for those and any other key
  group on a SQL fragment with a literal key. Inlined keys vary the statement
  text per key, so pass only keys from a fixed set, not user input.
- Filtered search: with iterative scan off, an ANN index returns its nearest
  candidates and applies `Where` afterwards, so a selective filter can return FEWER
  than `Limit` rows even when enough match. Set `HNSWIterativeScan`
  (`IterativeRelaxedOrder`; results stay approximate and can still be short when
  the filter matches fewer rows than `HNSWMaxScanTuples`).
- Small-table seq scan: below a few thousand rows the planner prefers a
  sequential scan, so `Explain` shows no index use in tests. That is correct. To
  check index use on a small table, run in a transaction:
  `tx.SetLocal(ctx, "enable_seqscan", "off")` then `query.Explain(ctx)` and look for
  the index name. `Tx.SetLocal(ctx, name, value)` sets any run-time parameter; never
  pass an untrusted name.
- Opclass mismatch or missing opclass for hnsw: see above.
- Index-less exact search (`ExactSearch`) is for measuring recall or small tables.
- Binary wire codec is opt-in (`pgxdriver.ConfigureVectors(cfg)` before
  `pgxpool.NewWithConfig`, then `pgxdriver.WithVectorFormat(pgxdriver.VectorBinary)`
  with a describe-based exec mode). Default text transport is correct; skip unless
  profiling says otherwise. `NewPool` does not call `ConfigureVectors`.
- Reciprocal-rank-fusion hybrid search does not exist; combine a distance and a
  text rank in one score instead ([fulltext.md](fulltext.md)).

Details: [vectors.md](vectors.md). Example: [vector-search](../examples/vector-search/).

## 10. Errors

Momo errors are `*momo.Error{Kind, Op, Table, Column, Constraint, Err}`. Check
with `errors.Is(err, momo.ErrX)` (matches `Kind`) and reach the driver error with
`errors.As` (for example `*pgconn.PgError`). `e.Detail()` returns the raw driver detail
(for PostgreSQL the key text) that `Error()` hides. `Detail()` is unmasked and can quote sensitive values: never log it or return it to a client. Never string-match error text.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
switch {
case errors.Is(err, momo.ErrNotFound):
case errors.Is(err, momo.ErrUniqueViolation):
	var me *momo.Error
	if errors.As(err, &me) { _ = me.Constraint } // which constraint
}
```

`me.Column` is empty for unique, foreign-key and check violations (PostgreSQL
reports a column only for NOT NULL). Use `Constraint` for those three.

| Error                    | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | What to do                                          |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `ErrNotFound`            | `One`, `First`, `Update.Model`, `Delete.Model` matched no row; `FindOrCreate` re-select miss. `All`/`Each`/`Iter` never return it                                                                                                                                                                         | map to 404 or create                                |
| `ErrTooManyRows`         | `One` matched more than one row; has-one load matched several children                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | fix the filter or the data                          |
| `ErrUniqueViolation`     | unique key or primary key violated (SQLSTATE 23505)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | conflict; `Constraint` names it                     |
| `ErrForeignKeyViolation` | FK violated (23503)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | missing parent or children still exist              |
| `ErrCheckViolation`      | CHECK failed (23514)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | business rule                                       |
| `ErrNotNullViolation`    | NULL into NOT NULL (23502); has-one/has-many `Unlink`/`Replace` on a NOT NULL FK                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | fix the data or nullability                         |
| `ErrSerialization`       | serialization failure or deadlock (40001, 40P01)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | retry the whole transaction with backoff            |
| `ErrBusy`                | lock not available (55P03)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | retry later                                         |
| `ErrOptimisticLock`      | `Update.Model` on a versioned model with a stale version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | reload, reapply, retry                              |
| `ErrUnfilteredMutation`  | `Update`/`Delete` without `Where` and without `AllRows()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | add a filter                                        |
| `ErrValidation`          | bad input detected before the database: wrong vector dim, `After` count, empty `Models`, writing a reserved/read-only column, plain `Delete` on a soft-delete model, negative `Limit`, `Link` with NULL key, bad `SearchSettings`, qualifier not in FROM                                                  | programmer or input error; fix the call             |
| `ErrUnsupported`         | dialect or driver cannot do it: `Each`/`Iter` with `Preload`; `Joined` shape; `LoadPerParentLimit` on to-one; belongs-to helpers; keyset on nullable key; `IndexedBy`; iterative search on pgvector < 0.8; simple protocol exec mode; non-standard isolation; transactions on a pinned conn; SQLite/MySQL | redesign the call; not retryable                    |
| `ErrAdoptedTx`           | `Commit` or `Rollback` on a `*Tx` from `AdoptTx`; the caller owns that transaction                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | finish the transaction with the caller's own handle |
| `ErrTxDone`              | `*Tx` already committed or rolled back                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | do not reuse a finished `Tx`                        |
| `ErrLimitExceeded`       | configured limit exceeded (for example one row has more columns than the bind limit)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | split or raise the limit                            |
| `ErrPinnedBusy`          | `Release` on a pinned connection that is still executing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | wait and release again                              |
| `ErrInvalidVector`       | a vector value failed validation (same value as `vector.ErrInvalidVector`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | fix the vector                                      |

Driver errors Momo does not classify keep their original type: reach them with
`errors.As(err, &pgErr)`. Data exceptions (SQLSTATE class 22, for example
invalid text representation) hide the message because it may quote the value; the
`*pgconn.PgError` is still reachable.

Migration errors (package `migrate` and the CLI, exit codes in section 5):
`migrate.ErrChecksumMismatch`, `ErrDirty`, `ErrLocked`, `ErrDestructive`,
`ErrBranchConflict`, `ErrStagedRequired`, `ErrBaselineMismatch`, `ErrNoSnapshot`,
`ErrNoDown`; `migrate.ErrNewerFormat` (a snapshot written by a newer momo).

Rules:

- DO use `errors.Is`, not `==` (errors are wrapped).
- DON'T retry `ErrUnique`/`ErrValidation`/`ErrUnsupported`; DO retry
  `ErrSerialization` (whole transaction) and `ErrBusy` (with backoff).
- DON'T return raw `*momo.Error` text to API clients; it names tables and
  constraints.

## 11. Testing apps that use Momo

Test against a real PostgreSQL with pgvector, not a mock. CI of Momo itself runs
`pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg16` and `0.8.7-pg17`.

Use the public kit `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/momotest` (see
[testing.md](testing.md)):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
//go:build integration

db := momotest.New(t, momotest.WithMigrations(app.Migrations()))  // schema per test, dropped after
tx := momotest.NewTx(t, momotest.WithMigrations(app.Migrations())) // rolled back after; Commit refused
momotest.Seed(t, tx, momotest.Insert(&org), momotest.Insert(&user))
```

It reads `MOMO_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` (skip when unset, fail when
`MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1`), is safe with `t.Parallel` and `-race`, and
`WithExtensions("vector")` creates the extension first. What it does, if you
need to do it by hand (the examples' own harness is internal to the Momo
module):

1. Read an admin URL from an env var (the examples use `MOMO_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`);
   `t.Skip` when it is unset (and `t.Fatal` when your CI sets a require flag).
2. Create a scratch database per test (`CREATE DATABASE t_<random>` over a plain
   pgx connection), connect `pgxdriver.NewPool` to it, drop it in `t.Cleanup`.
3. Apply your real migrations from code:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
import (
	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo/migrate"
	mpg "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/migrate/postgres"
)

db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool))
e, err := migrate.NewEngine(db.Driver(), os.DirFS("../migrations"), migrate.WithDialect(mpg.New()))
if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
if _, err := e.Apply(ctx, migrate.ApplyOptions{}); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
```

(The role needs permission to `CREATE EXTENSION vector`.) Pass the migrations
directory configured in `migrate.dir.postgres`. 4. Run the code under test against `db`; assert on results and on `errors.Is`. 5. Also run `momo generate --check` and `momo migrate validate` as tests or CI
steps.

What to mock and what not:

- DON'T mock `momo.DB`, `momo.Tx` or `momo.Querier`. `Querier` is sealed (it has
  unexported methods; you cannot implement it) and query builders are the code
  under test.
- DO hide Momo behind your own repository/service interface and fake THAT in unit
  tests of business logic.
- DO test queries, migrations, relations and transactions against real PostgreSQL.
- Use `WithClock(func() time.Time)` (`momo.New(drv, momo.WithClock(fn))`) for
  deterministic `created_at`/`updated_at`/soft-delete times.
- `WithMaxParams(n)` with a small `n` exercises chunking with little data.
- The `momo.Driver` interface can be faked, but the mock then proves nothing about
  SQL; prefer `Select...SQL()` golden checks for pure SQL-shape tests.

Examples: every `examples/*/example_test.go`, harness
[examples/internal/exampletest](../examples/internal/exampletest/exampletest.go).

### Observability and scoping helpers

- `momolog.New(logger, opts...)` returns a `momo.Hook` that logs one record per
  statement (op, table, relation, sql, duration, rows, err). Options: `Level`,
  `SlowOver` (statements slower than the duration log at WARN) and `Values`.
  Argument values are logged only with `Values(true)` and `momo.WithArgLogging`
  together.
- `momo.WithQueryScope(ctx)` groups statements for `momo.NewNPlusOneHook(threshold,
report)`, a development hook that reports once per statement shape per scope
  when the shape runs more than the threshold. Contexts without a scope are not
  tracked; a scope tracks at most 1024 shapes; a panic in the report function is
  recovered. A single batched relation load runs one statement per relation and does not trigger it.
- `momo.WithTenant(ctx, tenant)` and `momo.TenantFilter(ctx, column)` add a
  `column = tenant` predicate. This is an application-side convenience and NOT a
  security boundary. It applies only where you add it to a `Where`: not to
  Update or Delete, not to the tenant column of an Insert, not to Preload, Load
  or LoadCounts, joins, subqueries or raw SQL. A missing tenant, or one whose Go
  type is not exactly the column type, fails the build with `ErrValidation`
  (also under Not and Or). The zero value is a real tenant. Enforce isolation
  with PostgreSQL row-level security: it is configured by your own
  `WithTxSetup` function, which reads whatever your code put in the context. To
  drive both from `WithTenant`, read the tenant there and call
  `SetConfigLocal`. Without `WithImplicitTx`, non-transactional queries get no
  setting.
- `WithImplicitTx` and RETURNING writes: on an unpinned `*DB` configured with
  `WithImplicitTx`, read the rows of `Insert`, `Update` or `Delete` with
  `Rows` to the end (`for rows.Next() {}`) before `Close`. A write whose rows
  were closed unread, or after only the first row, is rolled back and `Close`
  returns `ErrValidation`. This also holds for a panic that unwinds through the
  loop, however `Close` is deferred. The library's own single-row helpers
  (`FindOrCreate`, `UpsertByPK`, `CreateGraph`) read to the end themselves. Handles
  without `WithImplicitTx`, `Tx` and pinned `OnConn` handles are unaffected.

## 12. Rules for AI agents

1. v0.3.0 is PostgreSQL + pgvector via pgx first; SQLite runs through the cgo driver `sqlitedriver` (not on Windows) or the pure-Go `sqlitepure` (no vectors); `momo migrate` is PostgreSQL-only (SQLite and MySQL migrations are library only: `migrate/sqlite`, `migrate/mysql`); the vector builders work on `sqlitedriver` only (via sqlite-vec); MySQL stores vectors only and MariaDB has distance functions; see docs/capabilities.md. <!-- x-release-please-version -->
2. Install the CLI at the same version as the library
   (`go install github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cmd/momo@v0.3.0`). <!-- x-release-please-version -->
3. Models embed `momo.Model` by value with `momo:"table:<name>"`; run
   `momo generate` after every model change and commit the generated files.
4. Never edit `*_gen.go`. Never hand-write `MomoMeta` for a table model or a
   projection.
5. Non-pointer field = NOT NULL; pointer = NULL-able. Use `SetNull()` only on
   pointer fields.
6. Use `Insert.Model` to store the struct as-is (zeros included); `Insert.Values`
   to fall back to database defaults. Use `Returning(...).Rows` to read identities.
7. Use `Update.Set(col.Set(v))` for partial updates, `Update.Model` for whole-row
   updates with a `version` column; handle `ErrOptimisticLock` by reload and
   retry. `Set` updates do not touch the version.
8. Never call `AllRows()` to get past `ErrUnfilteredMutation`; add a `Where`.
9. Soft-delete models: `SoftDelete`/`ForceDelete`, not `Delete`. Raw SQL and
   projections whose `From` is a subquery or a hand-built `TableRef` do not get
   the soft-delete filter: add `Where(<table>.DeletedAt.IsNull())` yourself. A
   projection read `From` a generated table (`Select[Card]`, the vector `Hit`)
   is filtered automatically; do not add the predicate.
10. Page with `OrderBy` + `After` and a unique tie-break; pass one value per
    effective ORDER BY key (primary key included).
11. Pass user input only as arguments to `momo.SQL`/`TypedSQL`/`Exec`/`Scalars`;
    qualify column names in raw fragments inside joins.
12. Inside `db.Tx`, use only the `tx` handle. Retry the whole transaction on
    `ErrSerialization` with jittered backoff; never retry inside it.
13. Check errors with `errors.Is` against the `momo.Err*` sentinels.
14. Load relations explicitly (`Load`, `LoadAll`, `Preload`); never assume a field
    is populated. `Scope` and `Then` chain on one relation:
    `rel.Scope(opts...).Then(nested...)`.
15. `Joined()` is belongs-to only; `Link`/`Unlink`/`Replace`/`Count` are not for
    belongs-to; helpers skip hooks and `UpdatedAt`.
16. `FindOrCreate` and `OnConflict` need a matching UNIQUE constraint; many-to-many
    join tables need a unique key. A partial unique index needs
    `OnConflict(cols).Where(indexPredicate)`; a conditional DO UPDATE uses
    `.DoUpdate(...).Where(...)`.
17. Vector columns take `dim:<n>`; leave it off a `vector` or `halfvec` field only
    for a dimensionless column (embedding size depends on the model, rows
    filtered by a dims column; no hnsw/ivfflat index on it). hnsw/ivfflat indexes
    need an explicit opclass matching the distance function used in queries;
    ivfflat needs `lists`.
18. Run vector queries that need tuning inside `db.WithSearch` and use `tx`
    there; use iterative scan for filtered ANN searches; expect seq scans on small
    tables.
19. Migrations: `diff`, review SQL, commit all files, `apply`. Never edit an
    applied migration; undo with a new one. The CLI has no rollback.
20. NOT NULL additions without a default: `diff --stage`, apply, backfill, check
    no NULLs remain, then `diff --enforce-not-null` (or give the column a
    default).
21. Declare `Concurrently()` on large-table indexes. `-- momo:destructive` is
    informational; only `diff --allow-destructive` guards drops.
22. CI must run `momo generate --check`, `momo migrate validate` and the
    `diff ci_probe | grep -qx 'no changes'` probe; `apply` also refuses forks and
    out-of-order versions, but fail the pull request earlier.
23. Run `momo migrate` over a direct connection, URL from the environment, never
    `--url` (or `--url -` for stdin). Use `sslmode=verify-full` for remote
    databases.
24. Behind PgBouncer keep the default exec mode; never select the simple
    protocol.
25. Test against real PostgreSQL with pgvector; do not mock `momo.Querier`.


# Source: agents.md

# Using these docs with an AI coding agent

Momo is meant to be written by agents as well as people. The documentation is
built so an agent can read it without scraping HTML.

## Where an agent should read

- [Agent guide](ai-guide.md): one self-contained file with setup, modeling,
  migrations, queries, relations, vectors, errors, testing and the rules. If an
  agent reads one page, it reads this one.
- `llms.txt` on the documentation site lists every page with a link to its raw
  Markdown. `llms-full.txt` contains the Markdown of every page in one file.
  Each page also has a raw `.md` twin next to its HTML. All three are generated
  at build time and exist under every published version of the site.
- The repository root has its own `llms.txt` for agents that read the
  repository instead of the site.

## Canonical patterns

The shapes below are the ones the guide teaches. The linked examples run
against PostgreSQL in CI.

- Describe a table as a struct that embeds `momo.Model`, run `momo generate`,
  and build queries from the generated descriptors. See
  [getting started](getting-started.md) and the
  [quickstart example](../examples/quickstart/).
- Insert with `Insert[T]` and `Model`, read with `Select[T]` and `Where`, change
  rows with `Update[T]` and `Set`, remove them with `Delete[T]` or `SoftDelete`.
  See [crud-zero-null](../examples/crud-zero-null/).
- Run related statements in `db.Tx` and use the `tx` it passes in. See
  [transactions](../examples/transactions/).
- Load relations explicitly with `Load`, `LoadAll` or `Preload`. See
  [relations](relations.md).
- Change a schema by editing the model and running `momo migrate diff`, then
  review the SQL it wrote. See [migrations](migrations.md).

## AGENTS.md snippet

Copy the block below into the `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) of a repository that
uses Momo. It is the short form of the rules in section 12 of the
[agent guide](ai-guide.md); a test keeps it complete.

<!-- momo:agents-snippet:start -->

```markdown
## Momo (Go ORM)

- PostgreSQL with pgvector is the only supported database for `momo migrate`; elsewhere it is the reference database. SQLite (cgo driver, not on Windows; vectors through sqlite-vec on that driver only) and MySQL 8.4, MySQL 9.7 and MariaDB 11.8 run queries and writes, and have library migration dialects (`migrate/sqlite`, `migrate/mysql`); check docs/capabilities.md before relying on a feature there.
- Run `momo generate` after every model change and commit the generated files. Never edit generated files.
- A non-pointer model field is NOT NULL; a pointer field is nullable.
- Pass user input only as arguments to `momo.SQL`, `momo.TypedSQL`, `momo.Exec` and `momo.Scalars`. Never build SQL by string concatenation.
- Never bypass `ErrUnfilteredMutation` with `AllRows`; add a `Where`.
- Check errors with `errors.Is` against the `momo.Err*` sentinels. Never match error text.
- Use only the `tx` handle inside `db.Tx`. Retry the whole transaction on `ErrSerialization`, never inside it.
- Never edit a migration that has been applied. Write a new one with `momo migrate diff`.
- Run `momo generate --check` in CI.
- Run `momo migrate validate` in CI.
- Test against a real PostgreSQL with pgvector. Do not mock `momo.Querier`.
- Full reference: https://azrtydxb.github.io/momo/latest/ai-guide.md
```

<!-- momo:agents-snippet:end -->


# Source: TYPE_MAPPING.md

# Go to SQL type mapping

This page lists which SQL column type Momo uses for each Go field type, what
survives a round trip, and where the edges are. The tables are checked by
tests: `TestTypeMappingDoc` fails when a row here disagrees with the generator's
type map or a codec's `SQLType`, and `TestTypeMapping` creates a column of each
documented PostgreSQL type on a live server and round-trips edge values through
it.

## How a type is chosen

1. A field whose type implements the codec contract (`types.Codec`: `Scan`,
   `Value` and `SQLType`) uses its own `SQLType`. This is how `types.TimeOfDay`
   and `types.Hstore` get their columns.
2. Otherwise the generator maps the Go type with its built-in table
   (package `gen/typemap`). A pointer and the `sql.Null*` wrappers map like the
   type they wrap: nullability is a column property, not a type property.
3. A Go type with no mapping (for example `uint64` or `map`) makes
   `typemap.Map` return an error wrapping `momo.ErrUnsupported`, which the
   generator reports at the field. Give the type a codec or declare the column
   yourself.

## Generated mappings

`N` is the `size` tag for `string` and the `dim` tag for vector types. A
`vector.Vector` or `vector.HalfVector` field without `dim` is supported: it maps
to the bare `vector` or `halfvec` type, a dimensionless column that holds
embeddings of any size (see [vectors.md](vectors.md#dimensionless-columns)).
`vector.SparseVector` and `vector.Bits` require `dim`. SQLite has no vector
types.
A slice of a scalar maps to the PostgreSQL array of its element type; SQLite
has no array columns, so the generator rejects them there.

| Go type                      | PostgreSQL                 | SQLite        |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------- |
| `int`                        | `bigint`                   | `INTEGER`     |
| `int8`                       | `smallint`                 | `INTEGER`     |
| `int16`                      | `smallint`                 | `INTEGER`     |
| `int32`                      | `integer`                  | `INTEGER`     |
| `int64`                      | `bigint`                   | `INTEGER`     |
| `float32`                    | `real`                     | `REAL`        |
| `float64`                    | `double precision`         | `REAL`        |
| `bool`                       | `boolean`                  | `INTEGER`     |
| `string`                     | `text`                     | `TEXT`        |
| `string with size:N`         | `character varying(N)`     | `TEXT`        |
| `[]byte`                     | `bytea`                    | `BLOB`        |
| `time.Time`                  | `timestamp with time zone` | `TEXT`        |
| `types.UUID`                 | `uuid`                     | `TEXT`        |
| `types.Date`                 | `date`                     | `TEXT`        |
| `types.JSON[T]`              | `jsonb`                    | `TEXT`        |
| `vector.Vector`              | `vector(N)`                | `unsupported` |
| `vector.HalfVector`          | `halfvec(N)`               | `unsupported` |
| `vector.SparseVector`        | `sparsevec(N)`             | `unsupported` |
| `vector.Bits`                | `bit(N)`                   | `unsupported` |
| `vector.Vector (no dim)`     | `vector`                   | `unsupported` |
| `vector.HalfVector (no dim)` | `halfvec`                  | `unsupported` |
| `[]string`                   | `text[]`                   | `unsupported` |
| `[]int16`                    | `smallint[]`               | `unsupported` |
| `[]int32`                    | `integer[]`                | `unsupported` |
| `[]int64`                    | `bigint[]`                 | `unsupported` |
| `[]bool`                     | `boolean[]`                | `unsupported` |
| `[]float32`                  | `real[]`                   | `unsupported` |
| `[]float64`                  | `double precision[]`       | `unsupported` |

The PostgreSQL type of `time.Time` can be changed for the whole project with the
`types:` section of `momo.yaml`, for example `types: {time.Time: timestamp(3)}`
for a database created by Prisma (see `naming: prisma` in ai-guide.md). Only
`time.Time` can be overridden; a `type:` tag on a field still wins, and SQLite
ignores the setting. `timestamp(3)` stores a wall clock without a zone, so
follow the `timestamp` notes below and pass UTC times.

On SQLite, `bool` is stored as 0 or 1, and `time.Time`, `types.UUID`,
`types.Date` and `types.JSON[T]` are stored as text. The SQLite column is what
the generator emits. The SQLite driver (`driver/sqlitedriver`, cgo, not on
Windows) reads text columns back into `time.Time`, `*time.Time`,
`sql.NullTime`, `sql.Null[time.Time]` and `types.Date`, whatever the column was
declared as.

## Codec-provided mappings

These types are not in the generator's table. Their own `SQLType` method names
the column; the generator's table is the fallback for everything else.

| Go type           | PostgreSQL | SQLite |
| ----------------- | ---------- | ------ |
| `types.TimeOfDay` | `time`     | `TEXT` |
| `types.Hstore`    | `hstore`   | `TEXT` |
| `types.TSVector`  | `tsvector` | `TEXT` |
| `types.TSQuery`   | `tsquery`  | `TEXT` |

`types.Hstore` needs the `hstore` extension; the vector types need `vector`
(pgvector). Momo never runs `CREATE EXTENSION` for you.

## Mappings you declare yourself

The generator never emits these columns, but the Go types work against them
when you write the DDL (or a migration) by hand. There is no SQLite column to
document because nothing generates one.

| Go type                 | PostgreSQL  | SQLite |
| ----------------------- | ----------- | ------ |
| `time.Time (timestamp)` | `timestamp` | `n/a`  |
| `string (decimal)`      | `numeric`   | `n/a`  |

## Edge values and behavior

Each statement below is asserted by a test against PostgreSQL.

- Integers: `math.MaxInt64` and `math.MinInt64` round-trip through `bigint`;
  `int` is 64-bit and maps to `bigint`. A value that does not fit the column
  (an `int64` above `math.MaxInt16` into `smallint`) is a database error, not a
  silent truncation. `uint64` has no mapping and is rejected when bound if it
  exceeds `math.MaxInt64`.
- Floats: `NaN`, `+Inf` and `-Inf` are legal `double precision` and `real`
  values and round-trip. Compare with `math.IsNaN`, since `NaN != NaN`.
- Strings: any valid UTF-8 round-trips, including quotes and backslashes (they
  are bound, never interpolated). PostgreSQL rejects U+0000 in `text`. A string
  longer than `size` is a database error on `character varying(N)`.
- `[]byte`: `nil` stores NULL; an empty non-nil slice stores an empty `bytea`.
- `time.Time` on `timestamptz`: the instant is preserved, the zone is not. A
  value written at `+05:30` reads back as the same instant in the server
  session's location, so compare with `Time.Equal`, not `==`. Precision is
  microseconds; finer digits are cut. Times before 1970 and year 9999 work.
- `time.Time` on `timestamp` (no zone): you store a wall clock. Pass
  `t.UTC()` and treat the column as UTC; a value in another zone is stored as
  its UTC wall clock.
- `types.Date`: stores the year, month and day of `Time` in its own location;
  it reads back at midnight UTC. Compare the date, not the zone.
- `types.UUID`: round-trips all 16 bytes, including the all-zero UUID.
- `types.JSON[T]`: encodes with `encoding/json`. An empty slice and a nil
  slice are different JSON (`[]` and `null`) and read back as such.
  Query it with `JSONText`, `JSONPath`, `JSONContains` and `JSONHasKey`. A
  nullable column holds either SQL NULL or the JSON literal null; an extraction
  is NULL for both and for a missing key, so test the column itself with
  `IsNull`. Grouping by an extraction works only for plain keys (letters,
  digits, underscore) and not on a sensitive column; see the AI guide pitfalls.
- `types.TimeOfDay`: nanoseconds since midnight, truncated to microseconds
  (PostgreSQL `time` precision); `86399999999000` is the last representable
  value, and a value outside one day is an error.
- `types.Hstore`: a nil `*string` value is an hstore NULL; keys and values
  with quotes and backslashes are escaped.
- `types.TSVector` and `types.TSQuery`: the server's text form, with the
  lexemes sorted and normalized, so write values in that canonical form to
  compare them with `==`. An empty tsvector reads back empty. Full-text
  expressions are PostgreSQL only (see docs/fulltext.md).
- `[]string` on `text[]`: elements containing commas, quotes, the text `NULL`,
  or empty strings round-trip; an empty slice reads back empty.
- Slices as arrays: only `[]string`, `[]int16`, `[]int32`, `[]int64`, `[]bool`,
  `[]float32` and `[]float64` map. `[]int` is not mapped, because its width is
  platform dependent; use `[]int64`. `[]string` with a `size` tag becomes
  `character varying(N)[]`. A nil slice binds as NULL, so inserting it into a
  `NOT NULL` array column fails with a not-null violation; pass an empty
  non-nil slice (it stores `{}`), or give the column a `default '{}'` and omit
  it. The array predicates bind a nil value list as an empty array, never NULL.
- Slices as arrays: only `[]string`, `[]int16`, `[]int32`, `[]int64`, `[]bool`,
  `[]float32` and `[]float64` map. `[]int` is not mapped, because its width is
  platform dependent; use `[]int64`. `[]string` with a `size` tag becomes
  `character varying(N)[]`. A nil slice binds as NULL, so inserting it into a
  `NOT NULL` array column fails with a not-null violation; pass an empty
  non-nil slice (it stores `{}`), or give the column a `default '{}'` and omit
  it. The array predicates bind a nil value list as an empty array, never NULL.
- Decimal: carry `numeric` as a string to avoid binary floating point. Values
  beyond `float64` precision round-trip exactly, and `numeric` also accepts
  `NaN`.

## Null handling

A column that can be NULL needs a Go type that can hold NULL: a pointer
(`*int64`), a `sql.Null*` wrapper, or a type whose `Scan` accepts nil.
Scanning NULL into a plain `int64` or into a codec from the `types` package is
an error, never a silent zero value.


# Source: projections.md

# Projections

A projection is a result type that is not a table: a subset of a table's columns, an aggregate, or a computed column such as a vector distance. You select it with `momo.Select[T]`, name the source with `From` and the select list with `Columns`. A projection is read only: it cannot be inserted, updated or deleted.

## Declaring one

Embed `momo.Projection` by value in a struct. Every exported field is one column of the select list, in declaration order.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Card struct {
	momo.Projection
	ID    int64
	Title string
	Score int64 `momo:"column:points"`
}
```

- The column name of a field follows the naming rule of the project (`naming:` in `momo.yaml`), as for model fields. A `momo:"column:..."` tag overrides it. The name is a label: the select list is positional and not aliased.
- Unexported fields and fields tagged `momo:"-"` are skipped. Relation tags are an error on a projection.
- A projection has no table, no primary key, no indexes and no `MomoConfig`. The generator does not add it to the schema, so it never appears in a migration.
- A field type must be one the generator maps (see [the type mapping](TYPE_MAPPING.md)). An unsupported type fails `momo generate` with a message that names the struct and the field, for example `projection Odd: field Value: Go type complex128 has no SQL mapping`.

## The generated metadata

`momo generate` writes, for each projection, a `MomoMeta` method and a `momo.Meta` value into the `momo_gen.go` of the package that declares it. `Columns`, `Ptr` and `Value` cover every field in declaration order. `Identity`, `Version`, `SoftDelete`, `CreatedAt` and `UpdatedAt` are all `-1`, because a projection has none of those columns. Do not write this by hand. A package that holds only projections gets a `momo_gen.go` too.

## Reading

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
cards, err := momo.Select[models.Card](q).
	From(article.Table).
	Columns(article.ID, article.Title, article.Score).
	OrderBy(article.Score.Desc(), article.ID.Asc()).
	All(ctx)
```

`From` takes the generated `Table` of a model package, an aliased table (`article.Table.As("a")`), a CTE or a subquery. `Columns` must list as many expressions as the struct has fields, in field order. Without `Columns` the query fails with `ErrValidation`. Computed expressions (a distance, `momo.CountAll()`) are valid entries.

Keyset pagination over a projection lists the unique tie-break key in `OrderBy` yourself, since the metadata has no primary key. See [projection-pagination](../examples/projection-pagination/).

## Tuple rows: no struct per shape

For an aggregate, a join or a few columns that you read in one place, skip the struct and the generated metadata: `momo.Row1` to `momo.Row10` are generic projections with fields `C1` to `Cn`. `Columns` is scanned positionally, so expression `i` fills `Ci`.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// a count per key
rows, err := momo.Select[momo.Row2[string, int64]](db).
	From(license.Table).
	Columns(license.Key, momo.CountAll()).
	GroupBy(license.Key).
	All(ctx)
for _, r := range rows {
	fmt.Println(r.C1, r.C2) // key, count
}

// a single aggregate
total, err := momo.Select[momo.Row1[int64]](db).From(license.Table).Columns(momo.CountAll()).One(ctx)
// total.C1
```

- A column that can be NULL takes a pointer type: a `LeftJoin` side or an aggregate over no rows. With a `Row3` of `string, *int64, *string`, the columns `a.Title, b.ID, b.Title` fill `C1` to `C3`, and `C2` and `C3` stay nil when the join finds no row.
- Subquery columns, `Union`, `FromSubquery`, `With` and `WithRecursive` work as for any projection. The Go types of the columns are yours to match; they are not checked against the SQL.
- A mismatch between the number of `Columns` and the arity of the row is `ErrValidation`, reported before any statement runs. So is omitting `Columns`.
- A tuple row is a projection with no table: `Insert`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Upsert`, `SoftDelete` and `ForceDelete` refuse it with `ErrValidation`. It has no soft-delete column of its own, and the filter on the `From` table applies as described below, so a `Row1[int64]` with `CountAll` over `article.Table` counts live rows, and `WithDeleted` counts all.
- `After` works when `OrderBy` lists a unique key, since a tuple has no primary key to break ties.
- The metadata is built once per instantiation and shared; looking it up does not allocate.

When the result has meaning worth a name, or more than ten columns, declare a projection struct instead and let `momo generate` write its metadata.

## Soft-deleted rows

When `From` is the generated `Table` of a model that has a soft-delete column (timestamp, unix or bool), a projection excludes soft-deleted rows by default, exactly as a model query does. `WithDeleted()` includes them and `OnlyDeleted()` returns only them. Do not add the `deleted_at` predicate by hand.

The filter applies to the `From` table whatever else the query does: with `Join` or `LeftJoin` the `From` table is still filtered, and the joined tables are not (filter them in the `ON` clause or a `Where`, as for a model). To alias the table keep the generated one and call `As`: `article.Table.As("a")` keeps the soft-delete column, so the filter is qualified with the alias.

The filter is not added when:

- `From` is a subquery or CTE: filter inside it;
- `From` is a hand-built `momo.TableRef{Name: ..., Alias: ...}`: it carries no soft-delete column. Start from the generated `article.Table` instead, or add the predicate yourself, for example `Where(article.DeletedAt.IsNull())`.

## Upgrading from hand-written metadata

Before the generator emitted projections, the guides told you to write `MomoMeta` and a `momo.Meta` value for each projection by hand. After you upgrade, `momo generate` writes them too, and the package no longer compiles (`MomoMeta redeclared`). Delete the hand-written `MomoMeta` method and its `Meta` variable for every struct that embeds `momo.Projection`, then run `momo generate`. Check that the field order and `momo:"column:..."` tags give the column names you had. Remove any `Where(<table>.DeletedAt.IsNull())` you added to projection queries; keeping it is harmless but redundant.

## Examples

- [projection-pagination](../examples/projection-pagination/): `Card` and an aggregate projection, keyset pagination, counting.
- [vector-search](../examples/vector-search/): `Hit`, a title together with its distance.


# Source: relations.md

# Relations

This guide covers how Momo models relations between tables: declaring them,
loading them, filtering by them, writing them, and observing them. Every
snippet uses the real API. The models are a small document store: `Document`
belongs to an `Author`, has many `Comment`s, and is tagged with many `Tag`s.

Relation operations are methods and functions on the generated `Relation[P, C]`
descriptor, where `P` is the parent model and `C` the child model. A descriptor
is immutable and safe for concurrent use.

- [Declaring relations](#1-declaring-relations)
- [Eager loading](#2-eager-loading)
- [Preload and single-query loading](#3-preload-and-single-query-loading)
- [Pipelined loading](#4-pipelined-loading)
- [Relation predicates and traversal](#5-relation-predicates-and-traversal)
- [Association helpers](#6-association-helpers)
- [Graph writes](#7-graph-writes)
- [Observability](#8-observability)
- [Errors and limitations](#9-errors-and-limitations)

## 1. Declaring relations

A relation is a field on the parent model. Its tag names the kind, and the Go
type of the field decides the shape:

| Tag          | Field type | Foreign key lives on |
| ------------ | ---------- | -------------------- |
| `belongs_to` | `*Target`  | the parent           |
| `has_one`    | `*Target`  | the child            |
| `has_many`   | `[]Target` | the child            |
| `many2many`  | `[]Target` | a join table         |

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Author struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:authors"`
	ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Name       string

	Documents []Document `momo:"has_many,fk:AuthorID"`
}

type Document struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:documents"`
	ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
	AuthorID   *int64
	Title      string

	Author   *Author   `momo:"belongs_to,fk:AuthorID"`
	Comments []Comment `momo:"has_many,fk:DocumentID"`
	Tags     []Tag     `momo:"many2many,join:taggings"`
}

type Comment struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:comments"`
	ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
	DocumentID int64
	Body       string
	Approved   bool
}

type Tag struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:tags"`
	ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Name       string
}
```

The generated code lives in one package per model (`author`, `document`,
`comment`, `tag`), imported next to the `models` package.

### Generating relation code

Run `momo generate` in the module that holds your models (or add
`//go:generate momo generate` to a source file and run `go generate ./...`).
It reads `momo.yaml` and writes the descriptors into the model packages. Commit
the generated files, and use `momo generate --check` in CI to catch stale ones.
The README walks through the setup in
[Configure and generate](../README.md#2-configure-and-generate). The join
tables and foreign keys come from `momo migrate diff` and `momo migrate apply`,
see [Create and apply the migration](../README.md#3-create-and-apply-the-migration).

Tag options for relations:

- `fk:<Field>` is required for `belongs_to`, `has_one` and `has_many`. For
  `belongs_to` it names the foreign-key field on the parent (the model that
  declares the relation). For `has_one` and `has_many` it names the field on
  the child.
- `join:<table>` is required for `many2many`. The join columns are named after
  each model and its primary key column, for example `document_id` and
  `tag_id`. Rules:
  - Set `join:` (same table) on every many2many side you declare. The
    reverse side is optional, but a reverse side declared without `join:`
    makes the generator report a diagnostic.
  - A many-to-many to the model's own type is not supported.
  - Both models need a primary key.
  - The join table has exactly two key columns, named `<model>_<pkcol>`. Extra
    join-table columns are not modelled by this guide; use an explicit join
    model such as a `Tagging` struct for those.
- `polytype:<column>` together with `polyvalue:<value>` makes a `has_one` or
  `has_many` polymorphic: the child row belongs to the parent only when its
  type column equals the value.
- `on_delete`, `on_update` and `no_constraint` affect only the foreign key
  emitted for `belongs_to`. `has_one` and `has_many` create no constraint, and
  many-to-many join tables always get two foreign keys with
  `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

`momo generate` reads these tags and writes one descriptor per relation field
into the model's package. The descriptor holds the relation name and kind, the
parent and child tables, the key columns, `Through` for the join table of a
many-to-many relation, `Discriminator` for a polymorphic one, and the typed
functions that read and write keys and the field itself. You refer to a
relation as `<model package>.<Field>`:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
document.Author   // belongs-to: momo.Relation[models.Document, models.Author]
document.Comments // has-many
document.Tags     // many-to-many
```

The generator reports a diagnostic, and writes nothing for that package, when:

- a relation has more than one kind, or the field type does not match the kind;
- the target is not a Momo model;
- `fk` is missing, or names a field that does not exist;
- `many2many` has no `join:`, or a declared reverse side has no `join:`;
- `polytype` is given without `polyvalue` or the other way round, or
  `polytype` is used on a relation that is not `has_one` or `has_many`;
- the `polytype` column is not a field of the target.

A `belongs_to` is keyed by its own `fk` field against the target's primary
key, so the referencing model may have any primary key, including a composite
one that contains the foreign key column. For example `exams` with primary key
`(license_id, exam_id)` can declare `License *License` with
`momo:"belongs_to,fk:LicenseID"`, which emits a foreign key
from `license_id` to the `licenses` table's `license_id` column and matches a live
database that already has that constraint. The target of a `belongs_to` must
have a single-column primary key: a foreign key to a composite target key is
refused with a diagnostic that names the target's key columns. A `has_one` or
`has_many` needs a single-column primary key on the parent, and the child may
have a composite key. `many2many` needs a single-column primary key on both
models. Other composite-key relations work with hand-written descriptors but
cannot be expressed with tags.

Generated relation field values (`Document.Comments`) are only ever written by
Momo when you load them or list them for `CreateGraph`. A plain `Insert` or
`Update` never touches a relation field.

## 2. Eager loading

`momo.Load` loads one relation for a slice of parents and assigns the result
onto each element. `momo.LoadAll` loads several.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
docs, err := momo.Select[models.Document](db).Limit(20).All(ctx)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
if err := momo.Load(ctx, db, docs, document.Comments); err != nil {
	return err
}
if err := momo.LoadAll(ctx, db, docs, document.Author, document.Tags); err != nil {
	return err
}
```

The cost is one statement per relation (per bind-limit chunk, see
[Chunking](#chunking)), not one per parent. Parent order and length never
change. Parents with a NULL key get an empty association: a nil pointer or a
nil slice.

Behavior to rely on:

- Associations are cleared before anything is assigned. A parent that matches
  no children ends up empty rather than stale, and a load that fails part-way
  leaves empty associations, never partial ones.
- Soft-deleted children are excluded by default when the child model has a
  soft-delete column, as in `Select`.
- A to-one child shared by several parents is copied shallowly for each
  parent. Pointers inside the child, including relations loaded with `Then`,
  are shared among those copies.
- A has-one relation that matches more than one child for a parent fails with
  `ErrTooManyRows`.
- With no parents, `LoadAll` returns nil and runs nothing.

### Scoping a load

`Relation.Scope` takes load options for the child statement:

| Option                  | Effect                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LoadWhere[C]`          | extra predicates on the child table                                                                         |
| `LoadOrderBy[C]`        | child order; the relation key and child primary key are always appended as tie-breakers, so order is stable |
| `LoadPerParentLimit[C]` | keep at most `n` children per parent (top-N)                                                                |
| `LoadWithDeleted[C]`    | include soft-deleted children                                                                               |
| `LoadOnlyDeleted[C]`    | only soft-deleted children                                                                                  |

`Load` accepts the same options directly after the relation. Use `Scope` when
you pass the relation to `LoadAll` or `Preload`:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
err := momo.Load(ctx, db, docs, document.Comments,
	momo.LoadWhere[models.Comment](comment.Approved.Eq(true)),
	momo.LoadOrderBy[models.Comment](comment.ID.Desc()),
	momo.LoadPerParentLimit[models.Comment](3),
)

err = momo.LoadAll(ctx, db, docs,
	document.Author,
	document.Comments.Scope(momo.LoadPerParentLimit[models.Comment](3)),
)
```

`LoadWhere` filters before the per-parent limit is applied, so "the three
newest approved comments" is what the example above loads.

`LoadPerParentLimit` uses a window function, so the load stays one statement
per chunk. It needs PostgreSQL, MySQL 8, MariaDB 10.2 or SQLite 3.25 or later.
It applies to has-many and many-to-many relations only. On belongs-to and
has-one it fails with `ErrUnsupported`, and a negative `n` fails with
`ErrValidation`, both before any statement runs. Zero means unlimited. For a
many-to-many relation whose child has a primary key, duplicated join-table rows
share a rank and cannot use up the limit. Without a child primary key, each
duplicated row takes a rank and can count against the limit.

`LoadWithDeleted` and `LoadOnlyDeleted` replace each other: the last one given
wins. They have no effect on a child model without a soft-delete column.

### Nested loads

`Relation.Then` loads relations on the children, in one pass over all children
of the level above:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
err := momo.LoadAll(ctx, db, authors,
	author.Documents.Then(document.Comments),
)
```

Nested loads run over the children that were kept, so combined with a
per-parent limit they only load for the survivors.

`Scope` and `Then` combine on one relation. Both return a `RelationLoader`,
which has `Scope` and `Then` methods itself, so a filtered, ordered relation
with nested loads is one loader ("approved comments, newest first, each with
its author"):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
err := momo.LoadAll(ctx, db, documents,
	document.Comments.Scope(
		momo.LoadWhere[models.Comment](comment.Approved.Eq(true)),
		momo.LoadOrderBy[models.Comment](comment.ID.Desc()),
	).Then(comment.Author),
)
```

- API note: `Relation.Scope` and `Relation.Then` used to return `Loader[P]`
  and now return `RelationLoader[P, C]`, which implements `Loader[P]`. Passing
  them to `Load`, `LoadAll`, `Preload` or `Then`, or assigning them to a
  `Loader[P]`, compiles unchanged. Only code that declares a variable with the
  inferred type and then assigns a different loader to it needs a
  `var l momo.Loader[P]` declaration.
- `Scope(...).Then(...)` and `Then(...).Scope(...)` are the same loader. Calling
  either more than once accumulates: predicates AND together, order items
  append, a later `LoadPerParentLimit` replaces an earlier one, nested loaders
  append. A `RelationLoader` is a value, so a base loader can be shared.
- The options apply to this relation's children only. Nested loaders carry
  their own options, so `author.Documents.Then(document.Comments.Scope(...))`
  scopes the comments, not the documents.
- The nested level runs once over exactly the children that survived the
  options, so the statement count stays one per bind-limit chunk at the top
  and one per level below it. A child excluded by `LoadWhere` is never a
  nested parent.
- With no options and no nested loaders a `RelationLoader` behaves like the
  plain relation. An error or cancelled context at the nested level is
  returned from `LoadAll`.

### Chunking

Parent keys are sent as bind parameters, and every dialect caps how many a
statement may carry. Momo splits the parent keys into chunks that fit under the
dialect's limit and runs one statement per chunk, so a load of any size works.
`WithMaxParams(n)` lowers the limit for a `DB`. Use it for tests that want to
exercise chunking with small data, or for databases configured below the
dialect's default:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
db := momo.New(drv, momo.WithMaxParams(100))
```

If a scope alone binds so many arguments that no key fits under the limit, the
load fails with `ErrValidation` before any statement runs.

### Counting children for many parents

`Relation.Count` counts one parent per statement. To show a count next to each
row of a list, `LoadCounts` counts all parents at once: one grouped
`SELECT key, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY key` per bind-limit chunk.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
counts, err := momo.LoadCounts(ctx, db, docs, document.Comments,
	momo.LoadWhere[models.Comment](comment.Approved.Eq(true)))
// counts[i] is the number of approved comments of docs[i]
```

- The result has one entry per parent, in parent order. A parent with no
  children or a NULL key counts zero; parents sharing a key share the count.
- Has-one, has-many (including polymorphic) and many-to-many relations are
  supported, with composite keys. Belongs-to fails with `ErrUnsupported`, as
  `Count` does.
- The load options that narrow the children apply: `LoadWhere`, and the
  soft-delete default with `LoadWithDeleted` and `LoadOnlyDeleted`.
  `LoadOrderBy` is ignored; `LoadPerParentLimit` fails with `ErrValidation`.
- Many-to-many counts join-table rows, like `Count`. The far table is joined
  when it has a soft-delete column and `LoadWithDeleted` is not set, or when a
  `LoadWhere` filter applies. Otherwise nothing is joined, so join rows whose
  far row no longer exists (dangling rows) are counted too.
- Parent keys are chunked under the dialect bind limit (see Chunking), and a
  relation hook sees one event per call.

To order or filter parents by their child count inside a query, use
`CountOrder` (section 5).

## 3. Preload and single-query loading

`SelectQuery.Preload` attaches loaders to a query. `All`, `One` and `First` run
