them after the rows are read, with the same statements `LoadAll` would use.
Preload returns a copy, so a base query can be reused, and a query with no
result rows runs no relation statement. Inside a transaction the loads run in
that transaction.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
docs, err := momo.Select[models.Document](db).
	Preload(document.Author, document.Comments.Scope(
		momo.LoadPerParentLimit[models.Comment](3))).
	Limit(20).
	All(ctx)
```

`Each` and `Iter` stream rows without collecting them, so they cannot batch
relation loads. With preloads they return `ErrUnsupported`.

### Joined

`Relation.Joined()` folds a belongs-to relation into the parent statement as a
LEFT JOIN, so it costs no extra round trip. Pass it to `Preload`. It does not
work with `Load`, `LoadAll`, `Scope` or `Then`. A matched joined child with
NULL in a column its Go field cannot hold fails with `ErrValidation` and an
error naming the child column (`column=...`).

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
docs, err := momo.Select[models.Document](db).
	Preload(document.Author.Joined(), document.Comments).
	Limit(20).
	All(ctx)
```

Here `Author` arrives with the document rows, and `Comments` is still loaded
with a second statement. Restrictions:

- To-one belongs-to only, and only when the relation's child key is the child's
  primary key or a single unique column. That is what guarantees the join
  cannot multiply parent rows, so `Limit`, `Offset`, `OrderBy` and `Where` of
  the parent query keep their meaning. Has-one, has-many and many-to-many fail
  with `ErrUnsupported` when the query runs.
- Not with `GroupBy`, `Having` or row locking on the same query (`FOR UPDATE`
  cannot lock the nullable side of an outer join), and not with `Each` or
  `Iter`. All of these return `ErrUnsupported`.
- If the query sets its own select list with `Columns`, it must have one
  expression per mapped field, or the query fails with `ErrValidation`.
- The parent's columns are qualified by the parent table in the select list, so
  a raw, unqualified column name in the parent's `Where` can become ambiguous
  with the joined table's columns. Qualify raw column names.
- Semantics match `Load` for belongs-to: a NULL foreign key, or a key that
  matches no child, leaves the field nil (never a zero struct), soft-deleted
  children are excluded by a condition in the `ON` clause so the parent row
  survives, and each parent gets its own copy of a shared child.
- A joined load runs no statement of its own, so it emits no `RelationEvent`.
  The parent statement is reported to the query hook as usual.

## 4. Pipelined loading

`LoadAll` (and so `Load` and `Preload`) works in levels: the top level holds
the relations you listed, and each `Then` adds a level. On a connection whose
driver implements `Batcher`, which the pgx driver does on the pool, on a
transaction and on a pinned connection, all statements of a level, including
every bind-limit chunk, are sent in one round trip. Other drivers (the
`database/sql` adapters, SQLite, MySQL) load sequentially. The result is the
same either way. There is nothing to enable and no per-call opt-out.

Two differences to know about:

- Memory. A pipelined level buffers all of its child rows before assigning any,
  so peak memory is roughly twice that of sequential loading, which holds one
  relation's rows at a time. Large child sets with a per-parent limit or a
  `LoadWhere` stay cheap; an unscoped load of a huge has-many does not.
- Hook event order. Sequential loading interleaves each relation's events with
  its statements. A pipelined level reports `BeforeRelation` for every
  relation, then `BeforeQuery` for every statement and one round trip, then
  `AfterQuery` per statement as result sets are read, then nested loads,
  assignment and `AfterRelation` per relation. The batch runs under the context
  of the first statement's hooks, so cancelling that context stops the whole
  batch, and a statement's `AfterQuery` duration includes its wait for the
  batch.

A batch is all or nothing: if one statement fails, every relation's
`AfterRelation` reports the error and the parents keep the empty associations.
If the driver rejects the batch before sending anything (`ErrUnsupported` with
`Op` `"batch"`), Momo falls back to sequential loading for that level.

## 5. Relation predicates and traversal

Relations also filter and order queries without loading anything.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
// Documents with at least one approved comment.
withApproved := momo.Select[models.Document](db).
	Where(document.Comments.Has(comment.Approved.As("momo_r").Eq(true)))

// Documents without any comments.
quiet := momo.Select[models.Document](db).Where(document.Comments.HasNo())

// Documents ordered by number of comments, most-commented first.
busy := momo.Select[models.Document](db).
	OrderBy(document.Comments.CountOrder(momo.DirDesc), document.ID.Asc())
```

- `Has(scope...)` renders `EXISTS (...)` over the child table, correlated with
  the parent through the relation's key columns. It is always a subquery, never
  a join, so it cannot duplicate parent rows.
- `HasNo(scope...)` renders `NOT EXISTS`.
- `HasFrom(parentAlias, scope...)` is `Has` with an explicit parent alias.
  Self-referencing relations need it: when the outer query aliases the parent
  table, pass that alias so the subquery correlates with the right instance.
- `CountOrder(dir)` orders parents by their number of children, using a
  correlated `COUNT(*)`. `dir` is `momo.DirAsc` or `momo.DirDesc`.
- Soft-deleted children do not count. For many-to-many relations the join table
  gets no soft-delete filter: only the child table's marker applies.

Scope predicates must name the child through the alias `momo_r`, because the
subquery owns that alias. Build them with `As` on the generated column:
`comment.Approved.As("momo_r").Eq(true)`. A predicate that uses the column
without the alias refers to the outer query's table.

`Relation.From(parents)` goes the other way: it returns a `SelectQuery[C]` of
the children whose key is in the key set of the given parent query. The parent
query is embedded as a subquery, so no parent row is fetched:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
comments := document.Comments.From(
	momo.Select[models.Document](db).Where(document.ID.Eq(int64(1))))
rows, err := comments.All(ctx)
```

`From` does not support many-to-many relations. The returned query fails with
`ErrValidation` when it runs.

## 6. Association helpers

`Link`, `Unlink`, `Replace` and `Count` write and count the link itself, with
no model in between:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
doc := models.Document{ID: 1}
tags := []*models.Tag{{ID: 1}, {ID: 2}}

err := document.Tags.Link(ctx, db, &doc, tags...)    // add pairs
err = document.Tags.Unlink(ctx, db, &doc, tags[0])   // remove one pair
err = document.Tags.Replace(ctx, db, &doc, tags[1])  // make this the whole set
n, err := document.Tags.Count(ctx, db, &doc)         // how many are linked
```

They only need the keys of the parent and children. They never modify the
values you pass in.

**They write SQL directly.** Model hooks, field hooks and an `UpdatedAt`
column are not touched. Use the model's own update path when those must run.

Statement contract, per relation kind (one statement per chunk; a small call is
one statement):

| Call      | Has-one, has-many                                                                                                       | Many-to-many                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Link`    | `UPDATE child SET fk = ? WHERE pk IN (...)`; a polymorphic relation also sets the discriminator                         | `INSERT` into the join table that skips existing pairs (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; MySQL `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` with a no-op); relies on a primary or unique key over the join columns |
| `Unlink`  | `UPDATE child SET fk = NULL WHERE fk = ? AND pk IN (...)`; a polymorphic relation also adds the discriminator predicate | `DELETE FROM join WHERE parent cols = ? AND (child cols) IN (...)`                                                                                                                       |
| `Replace` | diff, then unlink the removed and link the added                                                                        | same                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Count`   | `SELECT COUNT(*)` over the children                                                                                     | counts join rows, joined to the far table when it has a soft-delete column                                                                                                               |

What this means in practice:

- **Join tables need a unique key.** Many-to-many `Link` relies on a primary or
  unique key over the join columns to detect an existing pair. Join tables
  generated from `many2many` tags already have a composite primary key over the
  two columns, plus two foreign keys with `ON DELETE CASCADE`. A hand-written
  join table needs a primary or unique key too, or `Link` inserts duplicate
  rows.
- **Has-one and has-many `Unlink` and `Replace` need a nullable foreign key**,
  because they clear it. On a NOT NULL column they fail with
  `ErrNotNullViolation`, with a message saying so. Delete the children instead
  if they cannot exist without a parent. For the same reason they cannot be
  used when the child's foreign key column is part of its primary key (for
  example `exams` keyed by `license_id, exam_id`): the database rejects the
  NULL. Delete those children instead.
- **`Replace` is a transaction.** On a `*DB` it opens one, on a `*Tx` it runs in
  a savepoint. With no children it clears the set in one statement. Otherwise
  it reads the current child keys, diffs them in Go against the requested set,
  unlinks only the removed keys and links only the added ones, in chunks, so
  kept children are not rewritten and a set of any size works.
- **`Replace` locks the parent row** (`SELECT 1 ... FOR UPDATE`) on PostgreSQL
  and MySQL, so concurrent `Replace` calls on the same parent run one after the
  other. SQLite serialises writers and skips the lock. The lock is a row lock:
  a parent that does not exist locks nothing. On a `*Tx` the lock is held until
  the caller's transaction ends. `Link` and `Unlink` take no parent lock and
  can interleave with a concurrent `Replace`.
- **Belongs-to is not linkable.** Every helper returns `ErrUnsupported`. Set the
  foreign key on the parent and update it.
- **`Link`, `Unlink` and `Replace` return `ErrValidation`** when the parent key
  is NULL, or, for many-to-many, when a child key is NULL. `Link` and `Unlink`
  with no children are no-ops that issue no statement. `Count` of a parent with
  a NULL key is zero.
- **Chunks and transactions.** When `Link` or `Unlink` needs more than one chunk
  and the Querier is a `*DB`, the chunks run in one transaction, so the call is
  atomic. On a `*Tx` they run in your transaction without a savepoint. If a
  later chunk fails, the earlier chunks stay applied until you roll back.
  Chunk size follows the dialect bind limit, see `WithMaxParams`.

## 7. Graph writes

Graph writes are explicit. Nothing saves a relation you did not name.

### CreateGraph

`CreateGraph` inserts a parent and the children of the relations you list, in
one transaction. List relations with `Relation.Include()`:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
doc := models.Document{
	Title:    "Hello",
	Author:   &models.Author{Name: "Ada"},
	Comments: []models.Comment{{Body: "first"}, {Body: "second"}},
}
err := momo.CreateGraph(ctx, db, &doc,
	document.Author.Include(),
	document.Comments.Include(),
)
```

- Listed belongs-to children are inserted first and their key is copied into
  the parent. Listed has-one and has-many children are inserted after the
  parent, with the parent's key (read back with `RETURNING` when it is
  generated) copied into each child, and the discriminator set for a
  polymorphic relation. Many-to-many children are inserted and then linked
  through the join table. Relations are processed in the order listed.
- The graph is one level deep. Children's own relations are not followed, so a
  self-referencing relation or an in-memory cycle cannot recurse. A model that
  appears as its own child fails with `ErrValidation`.
- Every row goes through the ordinary insert path, so field hooks, automatic
  timestamps, Go-side defaults and validation run as for a plain `Insert`.
- Many-to-many children are always inserted, not looked up. A child that is
  already stored is inserted again and fails with `ErrUniqueViolation`, which
  undoes the whole graph. Link existing rows with `Link` instead.
- Has-many and many-to-many children are inserted with the chunked bulk insert:
  one multi-row statement per bind-limit chunk, so 1000 children cost one
  statement, not 1000. A has-one or belongs-to child is a single insert.
- The bulk insert's `RETURNING` rows are matched to the children in insertion
  order. If the database returns fewer or more rows than were inserted (a
  `BEFORE INSERT` trigger that skips a row, say), the graph fails with
  `ErrValidation` and is undone instead of leaving children without keys.
- A dialect without `RETURNING` (MySQL) returns `ErrUnsupported` before a
  transaction is opened.
- On a `*DB` the graph runs in a new transaction. On a `*Tx` it runs in a
  savepoint, so a failure undoes the whole graph and leaves your transaction
  usable. A dialect without savepoints returns `ErrUnsupported` there.

### FindOrCreate

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
a := models.Author{Name: "Ada"}
created, err := momo.FindOrCreate(ctx, db, []momo.ColumnRef{author.Name}, &a)
```

`FindOrCreate` inserts the model unless a row with the same key columns exists.
Afterwards the model holds the stored row, and `created` says whether this call
inserted it.

- **The key columns need a unique constraint.** The statement is
  `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING`, so the constraint decides the
  winner and concurrent callers never create duplicates; the losers re-select
  the winner's row. Without a constraint on exactly those columns the database
  rejects the statement. Dialects without `ON CONFLICT` or `RETURNING` return
  `ErrUnsupported` before any statement runs.
- When the row exists, all mapped columns of the model are overwritten by the
  stored values, and its relation fields are reset.
- A soft-deleted row is not "found". `FindOrCreate` never returns or restores a
  row you deleted, and it does not create a second row with the same key: the
  unique constraint still holds the soft-deleted row's key, so the insert
  conflicts and the call fails with `ErrUniqueViolation` (the deleted row is
  left untouched, and your model is not overwritten). This holds when the
  unique constraint covers soft-deleted rows, the case `FindOrCreate`
  supports. A partial unique index (`WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`) would let a new
  row in, but `FindOrCreate` cannot target it: its `ON CONFLICT (key)` has no
  index predicate, so the database rejects the statement. For keys that
  soft-deleted rows release, use `Insert` with `OnConflict(key).Where(...)`
  and `DoNothing`, then re-select. To reuse the old row, restore it first; to
  create a new one, use a different key. A model without a
  soft-delete column is unaffected. This is the least surprising choice:
  returning the deleted row would hand back data the application removed, and
  restoring it would undo a delete silently.
- Isolation. Under READ COMMITTED the conflicting insert waits for a concurrent
  transaction and the re-select then sees its row. Under REPEATABLE READ or
  SERIALIZABLE, the re-select can miss a row committed after the snapshot and
  return `ErrNotFound`. Retry the transaction in that case.
- An empty key, a key column the model does not map, or a nil model returns
  `ErrValidation`.

### UpsertByPK

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
err := momo.UpsertByPK(ctx, db, &a)
```

`UpsertByPK` inserts the model, or updates the row with the same primary key:
`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (pk) DO UPDATE SET col = EXCLUDED.col`. It is the
one-call form of `Upsert(q).Model(m)`. Generated columns are read back into the
model. The primary key, version, soft-delete and created-at columns are never
overwritten. Use the `Upsert` builder directly when the conflict target is a
different unique key, or when you want to choose which columns update.

## 8. Observability

A hook registered with `WithHook` that also implements `RelationHook` receives
one event per relation load:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type relLogger struct{ momo.Hook } // embed a Hook for the query events

func (relLogger) BeforeRelation(ctx context.Context, e *momo.RelationEvent) context.Context {
	return ctx
}

func (relLogger) AfterRelation(ctx context.Context, e *momo.RelationEvent) {
	log.Printf("%s.%s %s: %d parents, %d children, %d queries, %s, err=%v",
		e.Parent, e.Name, e.Kind, e.Parents, e.Children, e.Queries, e.Duration, e.Err)
}

db := momo.New(drv, momo.WithHook(relLogger{queryHook}))
```

`RelationEvent` fields:

| Field            | Meaning                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Parent`, `Name` | parent table and relation name                                           |
| `Kind`           | belongs-to, has-one, has-many or many-to-many                            |
| `Parents`        | number of parents the load ran for                                       |
| `Queries`        | child statements compiled for the load; a failed load may have run fewer |
| `Children`       | children loaded; set only when the statements succeeded, zero on error   |
| `Duration`       | filled before `AfterRelation`                                            |
| `Err`            | the load's error                                                         |

Events fire only for loads that execute statements. They do not fire when there
are no parents, when the load fails while being prepared (validation or
unsupported options), or for joined loads. `BeforeRelation` may return a derived
context, which later hooks and the load's statements see. For event order under
pipelining, see [Pipelined loading](#4-pipelined-loading).

## 9. Errors and limitations

Errors are `*momo.Error` values. Test them with `errors.Is(err, momo.ErrX)`.
The `Op` field names the operation.

| Operation                            | Error                 | When                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Load`, `LoadAll`, `Preload`         | `ErrValidation`       | negative `LoadPerParentLimit`; invalid descriptor; scope binds too many arguments for the bind limit                                |
|                                      | `ErrUnsupported`      | `LoadPerParentLimit` on belongs-to or has-one; `Each` or `Iter` on a query with preloads                                            |
|                                      | `ErrTooManyRows`      | has-one matched more than one child for a parent                                                                                    |
| `Joined`                             | `ErrUnsupported`      | not belongs-to, child key not unique, `GroupBy`, `Having`, locks, `Each`, `Iter`; used with `Load`, `LoadAll`, `Scope` or `Then`    |
|                                      | `ErrValidation`       | select list does not have one expression per mapped field                                                                           |
| `Has`, `HasNo`, `CountOrder`         | none of their own     | an error in the scope predicate surfaces when the query runs                                                                        |
| `From`                               | `ErrValidation`       | many-to-many relation                                                                                                               |
| `Link`, `Unlink`, `Replace`, `Count` | `ErrUnsupported`      | belongs-to                                                                                                                          |
|                                      | `ErrValidation`       | `Link`, `Unlink`, `Replace`: NULL parent key, or NULL child key on many-to-many. `Count` with a NULL parent key returns 0, no error |
|                                      | `ErrNotNullViolation` | has-one or has-many `Unlink` or `Replace` on a NOT NULL foreign key                                                                 |
|                                      | `ErrUniqueViolation`  | has-one `Link` that would break a unique foreign key on the child                                                                   |
|                                      | `ErrTxDone`           | the `*Tx` passed in is already committed or rolled back                                                                             |
| `CreateGraph`                        | `ErrValidation`       | nil parent, a model listed as its own child, a NULL key that must be copied                                                         |
|                                      | `ErrUnsupported`      | `*Tx` on a dialect without savepoints; identity read-back on a dialect without `RETURNING`                                          |
| `FindOrCreate`                       | `ErrValidation`       | nil model, empty key, unmapped key column                                                                                           |
|                                      | `ErrNotFound`         | re-select misses the winner's row under REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE                                                             |
|                                      | `ErrUniqueViolation`  | the key is held by a soft-deleted row                                                                                               |
|                                      | `ErrUnsupported`      | dialect without `ON CONFLICT` or `RETURNING`                                                                                        |
| `UpsertByPK`                         | `ErrValidation`       | nil model                                                                                                                           |

Database errors (unique, foreign key, check, not-null violations, serialization
failures) are classified the same way as for any other statement.

Known limitations and follow-ups:

- A tag-declared `belongs_to` needs a single-column primary key on its target
  (the referencing model's key may be composite); `has_one` and `has_many`
  need one on the parent; `many2many` needs one on both models. Other
  composite keys work with hand-written descriptors but cannot be expressed
  with tags.
- `Joined` covers belongs-to only. Has-one is not joinable.
- Pipelining has no public opt-out and doubles peak memory for a level.
- `Link`, `Unlink` and `Replace` bypass model and field hooks and `UpdatedAt`.
- `Replace` serialises concurrent callers only when the parent row exists, and
  `Link` and `Unlink` are never serialised against it.
- `CreateGraph` is one level deep and always inserts; it does not match
  existing rows.


# Source: vectors.md

# Vector search

Momo supports pgvector on PostgreSQL: value types, typed distance
expressions, HNSW and IVFFlat index declarations, scoped search settings,
plan inspection and an opt-in binary wire codec. It also runs the float32 and
bit vector builders on SQLite with sqlite-vec, and the distance builders on
MariaDB. This page describes what is built. Every Go snippet below is an `Example` function in
`example_vector_test.go` (package `momo`) or `vector/example_test.go`
(package `vector`), so `go test` compiles it and checks its printed output.

## Platforms and versions

- SQLite with sqlite-vec v0.1.6, through `driver/sqlitedriver` (cgo, not
  Windows); see [SQLite and sqlite-vec](#sqlite-and-sqlite-vec) below.
- PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension. Integration tests run against
  pgvector 0.8.7 (`pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg17` primary, `0.8.7-pg16` for an
  older major). The iterative scan settings need pgvector 0.8.0 or newer.
- The `vector` extension must be installed by a role that may create it.
  Momo never installs it at connect time. A missing extension surfaces as
  `momo.ErrUnsupported` from a migration, with the extension named in the
  message. A search settings call checks the installed version the same way.

## Not yet available

These parts of the vector plan are not built on this branch, so there is no
API to document yet:

- Hybrid search: PostgreSQL full-text plus vector search fused by reciprocal
  rank (planned options `TextCandidates`, `VectorCandidates` and `RRFK`, with
  k=60 as the default) does not exist yet.
- MySQL and MariaDB: see "MariaDB and MySQL" below. The migration engine for
  MySQL does not exist yet, so no tool creates VECTOR columns or indexes.

## Value types

The `vector` package holds the four Go types. Each has a `Validate(dim)`
method, a `Value` method that produces the pgvector text form and a `Scan`
method that reads it back. Validation errors wrap `vector.ErrInvalidVector`,
which the root package re-exports as `momo.ErrInvalidVector`.

| Go type               | PostgreSQL type | Notes                                                         |
| --------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vector.Vector`       | `vector(n)`     | float32, dimension 1 to 16000 (`vector.MaxDim`)               |
| `vector.HalfVector`   | `halfvec(n)`    | float32 in Go, float16 in storage, each value within 65504    |
| `vector.SparseVector` | `sparsevec(n)`  | `Dim`, zero-based strictly increasing `Indices`, `Values`     |
| `vector.Bits`         | `bit(n)`        | `Len` bits packed most significant bit first, trailing bits 0 |

Value rules, enforced before a value reaches the server:

- The length must equal the column dimension declared on the
  `VectorColumn`, unless the column is dimensionless (see
  [Dimensionless columns](#dimensionless-columns)).
- NaN and Inf are rejected.
- A halfvec component must satisfy |x| <= 65504.
- A dimension above 16000 is rejected for vector and halfvec.
- A sparsevec has at most 16000 stored elements (`vector.MaxSparseNNZ`) and a
  dimension up to 1,000,000,000 (`vector.MaxSparseDim`). Its text form uses
  one-based indices, as pgvector does, while `Indices` is zero-based.
- A bit string has at most `vector.MaxBits` bits, the PostgreSQL limit.

The `Example` functions `ExampleVector`, `ExampleHalfVector`,
`ExampleSparseVector` and `ExampleBits` in `vector/example_test.go` show the
validation and the text forms:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
v := vector.Vector{1, 2.5, -3}
fmt.Println(v.Validate(3))      // <nil>
text, _ := v.Value()
fmt.Println(text)               // [1,2.5,-3]
errors.Is(v.Validate(4), vector.ErrInvalidVector) // true
```

## Columns and distances

A `momo.VectorColumn[V]` is a typed column descriptor that carries the
declared dimension. Generated code emits one for every field of a `vector`
package type, with the dimension from the `dim` tag, so `document.Embedding`
passes straight to a distance builder. Build one by hand with
`momo.NewVectorColumn` only for a table the generator does not cover.

A vector column offers the predicates, ordering and write methods of a plain
column (`Eq`, `In`, `IsNull`, `IsNotNull`, `IsDistinctFrom`, `Asc`, `Desc`,
`Set`, `SetExpr`, `SetDefault`, `SetExcluded`), except the range comparisons
`Lt`, `Le`, `Gt`, `Ge` and `Between`: vectors have no meaningful total order,
so use a distance builder to order them. A nullable field (`*vector.Vector`)
gets `momo.NullVectorColumn`, which adds `SetNull`.

A vector field tagged `read_only`, `create_only` or `immutable` gets the
matching `ReadOnlyVectorColumn`, `CreateOnlyVectorColumn` or
`ImmutableVectorColumn`. They keep the write restriction of the plain
permission columns (no `Set` on a read-only column, an insert-only `Set` on
the other two) and every distance builder accepts them, so a read-only
embedding can be searched.

The distance builders take a column and a query vector of the same type.
Each returns a `DistanceExpr`, an `Expression[float64]` that works in the
select list, in comparisons and in `OrderBy`. `Asc()` orders nearest first
and is the default; `Desc()` orders farthest first.

| Builder                | pgvector operator | Column types            | SQLite function        |
| ---------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `L2Distance`           | `<->`             | vector, halfvec, sparse | `vec_distance_l2`      |
| `InnerProductDistance` | `<#>`             | vector, halfvec, sparse | none                   |
| `CosineDistance`       | `<=>`             | vector, halfvec, sparse | `vec_distance_cosine`  |
| `L1Distance`           | `<+>`             | vector, halfvec, sparse | `vec_distance_l1`      |
| `HammingDistance`      | `<~>`             | bit                     | `vec_distance_hamming` |
| `JaccardDistance`      | `<%>`             | bit                     | none                   |

`InnerProductDistance` is pgvector's `<#>`, which returns the negative inner
product so that ascending order means closest. Passing a dense vector to a
bit builder, or the reverse, does not compile (`testdata/compilefail`).

The query vector is a bound argument. A dimension mismatch (except on a
dimensionless column, see [Dimensionless columns](#dimensionless-columns)),
NaN or an out-of-range value is a build error wrapping `ErrValidation`, reported by
`SQL()` or by the first execution, never a server error. A metric the dialect
lacks is a build error wrapping `ErrUnsupported`. The metrics per dialect come
from `dialect.Dialect.Vector`:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
for _, name := range []dialect.Name{dialect.Postgres, dialect.SQLite} {
	caps := dialect.For(name).Vector
	fmt.Println(name, caps.Metrics, caps.Indexes)
}
// postgres [l2 ip cosine l1 hamming jaccard] [hnsw ivfflat]
// sqlite [l2 l1 cosine hamming] []
```

A nearest-neighbour query (`ExampleCosineDistance`):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
c, err := momo.Select[example.Document](db).
	OrderBy(momo.CosineDistance(document.Embedding, query).Asc()).
	Limit(5).
	SQL()
// ... ORDER BY ("documents"."embedding" <=> $1) ASC LIMIT $2
```

Reading the distance next to a column subset needs a projection struct
(`momo.Projection`, `From` and `Columns`; see [projections](projections.md)).
A projection read `From` a table with a soft-delete column gets the same
automatic filter as a model, so soft-deleted rows stay out of the results.
Add the predicate yourself only when `From` is a subquery or a hand-built
`TableRef`.

## Declaring vector columns and indexes

The generator maps `vector.Vector`, `vector.HalfVector`,
`vector.SparseVector` and `vector.Bits` fields to `vector`, `halfvec`,
`sparsevec` and `bit` columns. The `dim` tag sets the dimension, and
sparsevec and bit require it:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
Embedding vector.Vector `momo:"dim:1536"`
```

Generation adds `CREATE EXTENSION vector` to the schema when a vector column
or index is present. An ANN index needs an operator class, and pgvector's
hnsw has no default one, so declare vector indexes in `MomoConfig` (the
reference model is `internal/testmodels/example/models.go`):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
func (d *Document) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
	c.Index("documents_embedding_hnsw", &d.Embedding).
		Method("hnsw").
		Opclass(&d.Embedding, "vector_cosine_ops").
		With("m", "16").
		With("ef_construction", "64")
}
```

The generator and `schema.ValidateVectorIndex` reject an index that
pgvector would refuse, before any SQL runs. The error wraps
`schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex`. `schema.VectorIndexOpClass(type, metric)`
returns the opclass for a column type and metric (`ExampleValidateVectorIndex`).

### Index limits

| Method  | Types                           | Dimension limit                      | Opclasses (suffix after `<type>_`)        |
| ------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| hnsw    | vector, halfvec, sparsevec, bit | vector 2000, halfvec 4000, bit 64000 | l2, ip, cosine, l1; bit: hamming, jaccard |
| ivfflat | vector, halfvec, bit            | vector 2000, halfvec 4000, bit 64000 | l2, ip, cosine; bit: hamming              |

- ivfflat does not support sparsevec.
- hnsw accepts the storage parameters `m` (2 to 100, default 16) and
  `ef_construction` (4 to 1000, default 64, at least 2*m).
- ivfflat requires an explicit `lists` parameter (1 to 32768). Momo does not
  rely on the server default of 100.
- An index covers one plain column. Expression parts are rejected.
- Vector indexes exist only on PostgreSQL. Another dialect gets an error.

### Dimensionless columns

A `vector.Vector` or `vector.HalfVector` field without a `dim` tag maps to the
bare `vector` or `halfvec` type. Use it for a store whose embedding size
depends on the configured model: each row carries its size in a `dims`
column, and every search filters on it.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type KbChunk struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:kb_chunks"`
	ID         int64         `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Dims       int
	Embedding  vector.Vector // no dim: any size
}
```

- Generation emits a plain `vector` column and a `momo.VectorColumn` whose
  `Dim()` is zero. `sparsevec` and `bit` still require `dim`.
- A distance argument of any size is accepted; it is checked against its own
  size, so NaN, Inf and an empty vector are still rejected. The column never
  catches a size mismatch itself.
- pgvector fails a distance between two sizes, so filter on `dims` in the same
  query: `Where(chunk.Dims.Eq(len(q)))` plus `OrderBy(momo.CosineDistance(chunk.Embedding, q).Asc())`.
- The migration round-trips the bare type and the next diff is empty.
- Limit: pgvector cannot build an hnsw or ivfflat index on a dimensionless
  column. Momo refuses one, with an error that wraps
  `schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex` and names the column. Searches run as a
  sequential scan over the filtered rows. An expression or partial index such
  as `((embedding::vector(1536))) WHERE dims = 1536` is not supported yet:
  expression parts are rejected.

## Migrations

`migrate.Diff` emits the extension, the table and the index, and
`migrate/postgres` renders them (`Example_vectorMigration`):

```text
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "vector"
CREATE TABLE "documents" ("id" bigint NOT NULL, "embedding" vector(3) NOT NULL, ...)
CREATE INDEX "documents_embedding_hnsw" ON "documents" USING "hnsw" ("embedding" "vector_cosine_ops") WITH ("m" = 16, "ef_construction" = 64)
```

Inspection reads method, operator class and storage parameters back, so an
unchanged vector index produces no diff. A default operator class (ivfflat on
vector, `vector_l2_ops`) is stored as empty, which matches inspection.

## Search settings

`momo.SearchSettings` applies pgvector settings for one transaction. Zero
values leave the server default alone. Settings use
`set_config(name, value, true)`, so they revert at commit or rollback and
never reach a pooled connection, which makes them safe behind PgBouncer in
transaction mode.

| Field                   | Setting                                            | Range                                                           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HNSWEfSearch`          | `hnsw.ef_search`                                   | 1 to 1000                                                       |
| `HNSWIterativeScan`     | `hnsw.iterative_scan`                              | `IterativeOff`, `IterativeRelaxedOrder`, `IterativeStrictOrder` |
| `HNSWMaxScanTuples`     | `hnsw.max_scan_tuples`                             | 1 to 2147483647 (server default 20000)                          |
| `HNSWScanMemMultiplier` | `hnsw.scan_mem_multiplier`                         | 1 to 1000, float, a multiple of `work_mem`                      |
| `IVFFlatProbes`         | `ivfflat.probes`                                   | 1 to 32768                                                      |
| `IVFFlatIterativeScan`  | `ivfflat.iterative_scan`                           | `IterativeOff` or `IterativeRelaxedOrder`                       |
| `IVFFlatMaxProbes`      | `ivfflat.max_probes`                               | 1 to 32768                                                      |
| `ExactSearch`           | `enable_indexscan`, `enable_bitmapscan` set to off | bool                                                            |

`SearchSettings.Validate` reports a value outside its range as
`ErrValidation`. The iterative fields, `HNSWMaxScanTuples`,
`HNSWScanMemMultiplier` and `IVFFlatMaxProbes` need pgvector 0.8.0 or newer. When any of them is set,
`SetSearch` reads `pg_extension` and returns `ErrUnsupported` on an older or
missing extension, instead of letting the server accept an unknown setting as
a placeholder.

Use `DB.WithSearch` for a block, or `Tx.SetSearch` inside a transaction you
already have (`ExampleDB_WithSearch`, `ExampleTx_SetSearch`):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
settings := momo.SearchSettings{
	HNSWEfSearch:      100,
	HNSWIterativeScan: momo.IterativeRelaxedOrder, // needs pgvector 0.8
	HNSWMaxScanTuples: 20000,
	HNSWScanMemMultiplier: 2, // pgvector 0.8: iterative scan memory, times work_mem
}
err := db.WithSearch(ctx, settings, func(tx *momo.Tx) error {
	_, err := momo.Select[example.Document](tx).
		OrderBy(momo.CosineDistance(document.Embedding, query).Asc()).
		Limit(10).
		All(ctx)
	return err
})
```

`Tx.SetLocal(ctx, name, value)` sets any run-time parameter the same way.
Never pass an untrusted name: the name is bound, but `set_config` can change
`role` or `search_path`.

### Exact versus approximate search

An index scan is approximate. `ExactSearch` turns off index and bitmap scans
for the rest of the transaction, so a vector `ORDER BY` scans the table and
returns the exact nearest neighbours. The switches are not specific to
vector indexes: every other index lookup in that transaction also falls back
to a sequential scan, so keep the transaction short and dedicated to the
exact query.

### Filters, iterative scans and result counts

With a selective filter and `LIMIT k`, pgvector with iterative scan off scans
the index once and applies the filter afterwards, so it can return
fewer than k rows. `TestFilteredANNIterativeScan` reproduces this: a filter that matches 1%
of 20000 rows returns fewer than 10 rows with iterative scan off, and 10 with
`relaxed_order` and `HNSWMaxScanTuples` 20000.

`relaxed_order` keeps scanning until enough rows pass the filter or
`hnsw.max_scan_tuples` is reached. The result is therefore still approximate,
and it can be shorter than k when the filter matches fewer rows than that
bound allows. `strict_order` (hnsw only) keeps exact distance order while it
scans.

## Verifying index use

`SelectQuery.Explain(ctx)` runs `EXPLAIN` (never `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`), binds
the parameters and returns the plan text. It does not execute the query. Run
it inside the transaction whose settings you want to see
(`ExampleSelectQuery_Explain`):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
plan, err := momo.Select[example.Document](db).
	OrderBy(momo.L2Distance(document.Embedding, query).Asc()).
	Limit(10).
	Explain(ctx)
// look for "Index Scan using documents_embedding_hnsw"
```

`TestVectorIndexUsed` and `TestExactSearchBypassesVectorIndex` use this
pattern to assert that the index is used, and that `ExactSearch` stops using
it. Expect a sequential scan on a small table, because the planner prefers it
below a few thousand rows. Explain returns `ErrUnsupported` on MySQL.

## PostgreSQL wire format

By default vector values travel as text. The binary codec is opt-in and lives
in `driver/pgxdriver`:

- `pgxdriver.ConfigureVectors(cfg)` installs an `AfterConnect` hook that
  looks up the OIDs of `vector`, `halfvec` and `sparsevec` and registers
  codecs for them and for `bit`. Call it before `pgxpool.NewWithConfig`. The
  lookup runs once per connection: a connection opened before
  `CREATE EXTENSION vector` stays on text until the pool recycles it.
- `pgxdriver.WithVectorFormat(pgxdriver.VectorBinary)` asks for binary
  parameters. It needs a describe-based exec mode (`WithExecMode` with
  `pgx.QueryExecModeDescribeExec`, `CacheStatement` or `CacheDescribe`);
  pgx's default `QueryExecModeExec` always sends text, with identical
  results.
- `COPY` always uses binary and so needs `ConfigureVectors`.
- Decoders bound every length they read before they allocate.

`ExampleConfigureVectors` shows the setup:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
cfg, err := pgxpool.ParseConfig("postgres://localhost/app")
pgxdriver.ConfigureVectors(cfg)
pool, err := pgxpool.NewWithConfig(ctx, cfg)
db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool, pgxdriver.WithVectorFormat(pgxdriver.VectorBinary)))
```

## Differences between approaches

- pgvector exact search (`ExactSearch`) reads every row and returns the true
  nearest neighbours. Index search (hnsw, ivfflat) is approximate and tuned
  with `hnsw.ef_search`, `ivfflat.probes` and the iterative settings.
- sqlite-vec is brute-force KNN with no ANN index. A request for an ANN index
  on SQLite is `ErrUnsupported`. SQLite supports float32 vectors (l2, l1, cosine) and
  bit vectors (hamming) only; halfvec and sparsevec arguments, inner product
  and Jaccard return `ErrUnsupported` at build time. SQLite bit
  vectors keep only the packed bytes, so the declared column length is
  authoritative for `Len`. See [SQLite and sqlite-vec](#sqlite-and-sqlite-vec).
- `SetSearch` on SQLite: `ExactSearch` alone is a no-op, every search is
  already exact, and any other field is `ErrUnsupported`.
- MariaDB VECTOR INDEX is approximate; see "MariaDB and MySQL" below.

## SQLite and sqlite-vec

`driver/sqlitedriver` links sqlite-vec v0.1.6 (the version `vec_version()`
reports; `sqlitedriver.SQLiteVecVersion` is the release it is tested with, and
`Open` fails with `ErrUnsupported` on another minor or major version but accepts
a later patch release such as v0.1.7). The same typed builders that serve pgvector
render sqlite-vec's scalar functions, and the integration tests run them
against a real SQLite database: `vector_sqlite_integration_test.go` in the root
package and `TestSQLiteVectorParity` in `driver/sqlitedriver`. It needs cgo and
does not build on Windows. The SQLite migration dialect (`migrate/sqlite`) is library only, and the
generator refuses vector fields on SQLite, so you create the table with your
own DDL.

**Columns.** A vector is a plain `BLOB` column; sqlite-vec has no declared
dimension, so the length is guarded by a `CHECK`. `momo.SQLiteVectorType` and
`momo.SQLiteBitsType` return the definition to put after the column name:
`BLOB CHECK (length("emb") = 12)` for three float32 elements and
`BLOB CHECK (length("bits") = 1)` for eight bits. A vector of the wrong size
is then refused by the database as `ErrCheckViolation`. A dimensionless column
is `ErrUnsupported`, because there is no length to check.

**Values.** `vector.Vector` is stored as a little-endian float32 blob and read
back from one, and `vector.Bits` as its packed bytes (most significant bit first, as in
pgvector: bit 0 is the top bit of byte 0). Both are validated before
they are bound (NaN, Inf, an empty vector, a bad bit length are
`ErrInvalidVector`), because a blob has no text form that would reject them
later. A `*vector.Vector` or `*vector.Bits` field is nullable: nil binds `NULL`.
`HalfVector` and `SparseVector` have no sqlite-vec type, so binding one, or
searching with one, is `ErrUnsupported` when the query is built. A bit vector
read from SQLite has a `Len` of 8 times its byte count, so the column length is
the authority for a length that is not a multiple of 8.

**Metrics.** These are exactly the functions v0.1.6 registers:

| Builder                | SQLite function                                            | Column type     |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `L2Distance`           | `vec_distance_l2`                                          | `vector.Vector` |
| `L1Distance`           | `vec_distance_l1`                                          | `vector.Vector` |
| `CosineDistance`       | `vec_distance_cosine`                                      | `vector.Vector` |
| `HammingDistance`      | `vec_distance_hamming(vec_bit(column), vec_bit(argument))` | `vector.Bits`   |
| `InnerProductDistance` | none: `ErrUnsupported` at build time                       |                 |
| `JaccardDistance`      | none: `ErrUnsupported` at build time                       |                 |

The query vector is a bound argument. When the column is sensitive, it shows
as `momo.RedactedArg` in hook events, on a query and on an insert, while the
database gets the real blob. Distances work in the select list, in a
comparison and in `OrderBy` (`Asc` nearest first, `Desc` farthest first).
Results are held to the plain-Go reference in `internal/vectorparity`: the
top-10 ids of cosine, L2 and L1 search over 300 vectors equal the reference
exactly. The reference is the one pgvector exact search and MariaDB are held to
for cosine, and when a PostgreSQL URL is set `TestSQLiteVectorParity` also loads
the same vectors into pgvector and requires the same ids for cosine, L2 and L1.

**Indexes.** sqlite-vec compares every row, so it has no approximate index and
`dialect.For(dialect.SQLite).Vector.Indexes` is empty, and
`schema.ValidateVectorIndex` rejects an index for SQLite with
`schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex`. An internal check turns a request for any index
method on a dialect that lists none into `ErrUnsupported`; it becomes public
when a SQLite migration dialect needs it. SQLite itself does not parse an index method, so
nothing is accepted silently. `ExactSearch` in `SearchSettings` is a no-op (every
search is exact) and any other setting is `ErrUnsupported`. The sqlite-vec
virtual tables (`vec0`, which have an index of their own) are not wrapped.

Bring up a throwaway database for your own tests with
[`momotest/sqlitetest`](testing.md#sqlite-without-a-server-sqlitetest).

## MariaDB and MySQL

MariaDB 11.8 supports float32 vectors through `mysqldriver`. MySQL 9.x
stores them but cannot compare them.

| Capability                     | MariaDB 11.8                                                  | MySQL 9.7        | MySQL 8.4              |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- |
| Column type                    | `VECTOR(N)`                                                   | `VECTOR(N)`      | none: `ErrUnsupported` |
| `vector.Vector` write and read | yes                                                           | yes              | no                     |
| `L2Distance`                   | `VEC_DISTANCE_EUCLIDEAN(col, VEC_FromText(?))`                | `ErrUnsupported` | `ErrUnsupported`       |
| `CosineDistance`               | `VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(col, VEC_FromText(?))`                   | `ErrUnsupported` | `ErrUnsupported`       |
| Other metrics, other types     | `ErrUnsupported` (inner product, L1, halfvec, sparsevec, bit) | `ErrUnsupported` | `ErrUnsupported`       |
| ANN index                      | `VECTOR INDEX`, approximate                                   | none             | none                   |
| `Capabilities().Vectors`       | true                                                          | false            | false                  |

MySQL Community has no distance function (the distance functions belong to
HeatWave), so a distance query on MySQL fails at build time with
`ErrUnsupported`. Momo never falls back to a scan or to a Go-side sort.

A `vector.Vector` bound on MySQL or MariaDB travels as its text form wrapped
in `VEC_FromText` (MariaDB) or `STRING_TO_VECTOR` (MySQL), on every typed bind
path: insert, update, equality and distance. Stored vectors scan back from the
server's binary float32 form. A column marked sensitive masks the vector in
hook events exactly as on PostgreSQL.

A MariaDB `VECTOR INDEX` needs a `NOT NULL` `vector(N)` column and accepts
`M` from 3 to 200 and `DISTANCE` of `euclidean` or `cosine`. It serves only
the metric it was built with, and an `ORDER BY` distance with `LIMIT` uses
it. To get the exact nearest neighbours from the same table, add `+ 0` to the
distance in a raw query, which keeps the server from using the index.
`schema.ValidateMariaDBVectorIndex` checks a declaration and
`schema.MariaDBVectorIndexClause` renders it. `momo.MySQLVectorType` gives the
column type for a server version and refuses MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB before
11.7 with a diagnostic that names the version.


# Source: fulltext.md

# Full-text search

PostgreSQL full-text search has a column type and typed expressions in Momo.
Every builder here returns `ErrUnsupported` when the statement is built for
SQLite or MySQL.

## The column

A model field of type `types.TSVector` maps to a `tsvector` column (and a
`types.TSQuery` field to `tsquery`). Both are codecs, so the generator and
`migrate` pick the column type from the Go type, diff it and read it back from
the database with no drift. The Go value is the text form PostgreSQL prints,
for example `'cat':3 'fat':2`. A nullable column is a `*types.TSVector`.

The application normally never sets this column (leave it nil on insert and
update: the trigger overwrites it). Keep it current with a
trigger declared in `MomoConfig`, and index it with GIN:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Article struct {
	momo.Model `momo:"table:kb_articles"`
	ID         int64            `momo:"pk,identity"`
	Title      string
	Body       string
	SearchTsv  *types.TSVector
	Embedding  vector.Vector `momo:"dim:1536"`
}

func (a *Article) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
	c.Index("kb_articles_search_gin", &a.SearchTsv).Method("gin")
	c.Function(schema.Function{
		Name: "kb_articles_tsv", Returns: "trigger", Language: "plpgsql", Volatility: "VOLATILE",
		Body: "BEGIN NEW.search_tsv := setweight(to_tsvector('english', coalesce(NEW.title, '')), 'A') || " +
			"to_tsvector('english', coalesce(NEW.body, '')); RETURN NEW; END;",
	})
	c.Trigger(schema.Trigger{
		Table: "kb_articles", Name: "kb_articles_tsv_trg", Timing: "BEFORE",
		Events: []string{"INSERT", "UPDATE"}, ForEachRow: true, Function: "kb_articles_tsv()",
	})
}
```

## Expressions

The text search configuration (`english`, `simple`, ...) is a string. It is
bound as a parameter and cast to regconfig, so it cannot carry SQL; an empty
one fails the build with `ErrValidation`.

| Builder                   | SQL                                            | Result type              |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `momo.TSMatch`            | `vec @@ query`                                 | `Predicate`              |
| `momo.ToTSVector`         | `to_tsvector(config, text)`                    | `TSExpr[types.TSVector]` |
| `momo.WebsearchToTSQuery` | `websearch_to_tsquery(config, text)`           | `TSExpr[types.TSQuery]`  |
| `momo.PlainToTSQuery`     | `plainto_tsquery(config, text)`                | `TSExpr[types.TSQuery]`  |
| `momo.PhraseToTSQuery`    | `phraseto_tsquery(config, text)`               | `TSExpr[types.TSQuery]`  |
| `momo.ToTSQuery`          | `to_tsquery(config, text)`                     | `TSExpr[types.TSQuery]`  |
| `momo.TSRank`             | `ts_rank(vec, query [, normalization])`        | `TSExpr[float64]`        |
| `momo.TSRankCD`           | `ts_rank_cd(vec, query [, normalization])`     | `TSExpr[float64]`        |
| `momo.TSHeadline`         | `ts_headline(config, text, query [, options])` | `TSExpr[string]`         |

The query text, the configuration and the headline options are always bound
parameters. The normalization argument of the rank functions is the optional
PostgreSQL flag mask (0 to 63) and renders as a literal. `WebsearchToTSQuery`
accepts any user input without raising a syntax error, so it is the builder for
a search box; `ToTSQuery` expects tsquery syntax and a malformed query is a
database error.

A `TSExpr` has `As`, `Asc`, `Desc` and the comparison methods of any scalar
expression, so it works in Where, OrderBy and Columns:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
q := momo.WebsearchToTSQuery("english", userInput)
rank := momo.TSRankCD(articleSearch, q)

hits, err := momo.Select[Hit](db).
	From(momo.TableRef{Name: "kb_articles"}).
	Columns(articleID, rank.As("rank"),
		momo.TSHeadline("english", articleBody, q, "StartSel=<b>, StopSel=</b>, MaxFragments=2")).
	Where(momo.TSMatch(articleSearch, q)).
	OrderBy(rank.Desc()).
	Limit(20).
	All(ctx)
```

Here `articleSearch` is a `Column[types.TSVector]` and `articleBody` a
`Column[string]`. Without a stored column, search a text column directly with
`momo.ToTSVector` over `articleBody` as the first operand of `TSMatch` (an
expression index on the same expression keeps it fast).

Every use of a call binds its own parameters (the configuration and the query
text), so the same expression written in the select list and again in GROUP BY
gets different placeholders, and PostgreSQL rejects the statement as an
ungrouped column. The same applies to SELECT DISTINCT with an ORDER BY on the
call. Group by a stored tsvector instead, or compute the call once in a
subquery or CTE and refer to its alias. A golden test pins the placeholders.

Arguments bound by these calls are masked in hook events (shown as
`RedactedArg`) when an operand reads a column marked sensitive; the driver
still receives the real values.

## Hybrid ranking: vector plus text

Momo has no built-in fusion step (reciprocal rank fusion is not built). Combine
the two signals in one score with the typed arithmetic helpers. The cosine
distance is lower for better matches and the text rank is higher, so subtract a
weighted rank from the distance and order ascending:

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
dist := momo.CosineDistance(articleEmb, queryEmbedding) // vector.Vector
text := momo.TSRankCD(articleSearch, momo.WebsearchToTSQuery("english", userInput))
score := momo.SubExpr[float64](dist, momo.Mul[float64](text, 0.5))

hits, err := momo.Select[Hit](db).
	From(momo.TableRef{Name: "kb_articles"}).
	Columns(articleID, score.As("score"), articleTitle).
	OrderBy(score.Asc()).
	Limit(20).
	All(ctx)
```

This scores every row. To restrict the candidate set to text matches, add
a Where on `TSMatch` over `articleSearch` and the same query, which lets the GIN
index prune the rows before the vector distance is computed. The
`TestFullTextHybridRanking` integration test runs this pattern.

## Scanning

pgx returns tsvector and tsquery values as text, which `types.TSVector` and
`types.TSQuery` scan. `ts_rank` and `ts_rank_cd` return real; they scan into
`float64` fields.


# Source: mysql.md

# MySQL and MariaDB

What works on MySQL and MariaDB today, and what does not. The driver is
`driver/mysqldriver` (database/sql on `github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql`).
The migration dialect `migrate/mysql` exists as a library; the `momo
migrate` command is PostgreSQL-only (see [Migrations](#migrations)).

## Supported servers

| Server           | Version | Image used in CI |
| ---------------- | ------- | ---------------- |
| MySQL 8.4 LTS    | 8.4.13  | `mysql:8.4.13`   |
| MySQL 9.7 LTS    | 9.7.4   | `mysql:9.7.4`    |
| MariaDB 11.8 LTS | 11.8.9  | `mariadb:11.8.9` |

No innovation releases are supported. CI runs the shared suites against all
three servers (the `integration-mysql` job), on every push.

## Connecting

Open the pool with `mysqldriver.Open(dsn, flavor)`, or build the DSN with
`mysqldriver.ConfigureDSN` and pass the `*sql.DB` to `mysqldriver.New`. The
configured DSN always has:

- `parseTime=true` and `loc=UTC`, and the session `time_zone` set to `+00:00`;
- `clientFoundRows=true`, so an UPDATE reports the rows it matched;
- `interpolateParams=false` and `multiStatements=false`: values always travel
  as bound parameters of a prepared statement and never become SQL text. A DSN
  that sets either is overridden. A `*sql.DB` handed to `New` directly must
  already be configured this way.

`Open` pings the server, as the SQLite drivers do, so a bad DSN, a refused
connection or bad credentials fail at `Open` and not on the first statement.
An unknown flavor makes `Open` return `ErrUnsupported`; on any error the pool
is closed and nothing is returned. (`New`, which takes an already opened
`*sql.DB`, still returns a driver whose every call is `ErrUnsupported` for an
unknown flavor, because it has no error to return.)

`ConfigureDSN` (and so `Open`) refuses two DSN settings with `ErrValidation`:

- `allowAllFiles=true`, which lets the server read any client file through
  `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE`;
- `allowCleartextPasswords=true`, which sends the password unhashed.

Remove them from the DSN. The error message never quotes the DSN.

Transport security is the DSN's business and defaults to none: add `tls=true`
(or a registered TLS config) for any server that is not on the same host.

## Capabilities

The rows below are checked against `dialect.MySQLFlavor` by
`TestCapabilityMatrixMatchesDialect`.

| Capability       | mysql | mariadb |
| ---------------- | ----- | ------- |
| Returning        | no    | no      |
| InsertReturning  | no    | yes     |
| OnConflict       | no    | no      |
| OnDuplicateKey   | yes   | yes     |
| NullsOrdering    | no    | no      |
| TransactionalDDL | no    | no      |
| Merge            | no    | no      |
| ILike            | no    | no      |

`Returning` is the UPDATE and DELETE form. MariaDB 11.8 can return rows from an
INSERT only (`INSERT ... RETURNING`), which is why it has `InsertReturning`
set while `Returning` stays false: `Returning` on an insert works on MariaDB,
and on an update or delete it is `ErrUnsupported` on both servers. MySQL has
no `RETURNING` at all.

## Writes

- A single `Model` insert reads `LAST_INSERT_ID` and writes it into the
  identity field of the model. A key generated on the Go side (an id
  generator) always wins; `LAST_INSERT_ID` is read only for a key the database
  generates. A multi-row insert returns and writes back no keys, because the
  ids of a multi-row statement depend on `innodb_autoinc_lock_mode`. On MariaDB,
  ask for them with `Returning`; on MySQL that is `ErrUnsupported`. The
  `LAST_INSERT_ID` write-back does not apply to an upsert or to any insert with
  a conflict clause (`wantsGeneratedKey` in the core is false for them), because
  the statement may update an existing row and `LAST_INSERT_ID` then does not
  name the row's key; read the row back with a query.
- Upserts render as `INSERT ... VALUES ... AS momo_new ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`
  on MySQL and with `VALUES(col)` on MariaDB. `DoNothing` renders a no-op
  assignment of a key column. A `Where` on a conflict clause is
  `ErrUnsupported`.
- `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` fires for a conflict on any unique key and cannot
  name one. Momo therefore accepts a conflict target only when it is the only
  unique key of the table, the primary key included; otherwise the call is
  `ErrUnsupported`. Without a schema (a hand-written model) only a primary-key
  target is accepted.
- With `clientFoundRows`, an upsert reports 1 for an inserted row, 2 for an
  existing row that changed, and 1 for an existing row set to its current
  values. `DoNothing` also reports 1 for a skipped row. A count of 1 does not
  tell an insert from a skip.
- A bare `OFFSET` gets `LIMIT 18446744073709551615` in front of it, because
  MySQL and MariaDB reject an offset without a limit.

## Locking and transactions

`ForUpdate` and `ForShare` render `FOR UPDATE` and `FOR SHARE`; `NOWAIT` and
`SKIP LOCKED` are passed through. MariaDB 11.8 has no `FOR SHARE`, so it gets
`LOCK IN SHARE MODE`. `LockOf` (`FOR UPDATE OF`) is MySQL only; on MariaDB it is
`ErrUnsupported`. Savepoints and the four standard isolation levels work;
read-only transactions use `START TRANSACTION READ ONLY`. Any other isolation
level is `ErrUnsupported`.

## Errors

Server errors map by number: 1062 unique, 1451 and 1452 (and 1216, 1217)
foreign key, 1048 and 1364 not null, 3819 (MySQL) and 4025 (MariaDB) check,
1213 and MariaDB 1020 serialization (deadlock, and a row that changed under
`innodb_snapshot_isolation`), 1205 and 3572 busy. `Error()` never shows the
server text, which can quote a row value; `Detail()` returns it, and
`errors.As` reaches the `*mysql.MySQLError`. The constraint name differs by
server: MySQL 8 reports a unique key as `table.index`, MariaDB reports only the
index name.

## Vectors

MySQL 8.4 has no vector columns. MySQL 9.7 stores `VECTOR` and reads it back,
but offers no distance function in the Community edition (`DISTANCE()` is
HeatWave and MySQL AI only), so every distance builder is `ErrUnsupported` on
MySQL. MariaDB 11.8 renders `L2Distance` as `VEC_DISTANCE_EUCLIDEAN` and
`CosineDistance` as `VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE` on `vector.Vector` columns, and its
driver reports `Vectors`. Inner product, L1, Hamming, Jaccard and the half,
sparse and bit types return `ErrUnsupported` on MariaDB. Details and the
`VECTOR INDEX` rules are in [vectors.md](vectors.md#mariadb-and-mysql).

## Migrations

The library dialect `migrate/mysql` inspects `information_schema`, renders DDL,
locks with `GET_LOCK` and runs every migration, up and down, statement by
statement, because DDL commits implicitly on these servers. Build the engine
with `migrate.WithDialect` and the `mysqldriver` driver; the inspector, drift
check and `-- momo:ddl` online DDL options work through it. The
`momo migrate` command still builds only the PostgreSQL dialect, so it rejects
MySQL and MariaDB. What the dialect reports and renders is in
[migrations.md](migrations.md#9-mysql-and-mariadb).


# Source: migrations.md

# Migration safety and recovery

Momo v0.3.0, PostgreSQL (SQLite and MySQL as libraries, sections 3a and 9). Every statement here was checked against <!-- x-release-please-version -->
`migrate/`, `cmd/momo/`, `schema/` and `dialect/`; the tests that pin a
behavior are named. For the first run see README, [Create and apply the
migration](../README.md#3-create-and-apply-the-migration).

`momo migrate` runs PostgreSQL only; with another dialect it exits 2
("migrations for dialect ... are not available yet"). SQLite has a migration
dialect for use as a library, described in section 3a, and MySQL and MariaDB
have one described in section 9.

## 1. Model

```text
models (Go structs) --momo migrate diff--> <v>_<name>.up.sql + <v>_<name>.snapshot.json + momo.sum
                                              |
database <--------momo migrate apply---------+  (history table: momo_migrations)
```

### Files

All files live in one directory per dialect (default `migrations/postgres`,
set `migrate.dir.postgres` or `--dir`). `diff` writes exactly three files:

| File                             | Content                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `<version>_<name>.up.sql`        | Statements. Header `-- momo:generated`, plus `-- momo:destructive` and/or `-- momo:no-transaction` when needed. Statements are separated by a blank line and each ends in `;`. |
| `<version>_<name>.snapshot.json` | The whole schema after this migration, wrapped as `{format_version, version, parent, schema}`. `schema` carries its own `format_version`.                                      |
| `momo.sum`                       | Checksum manifest of every file in the directory, rewritten by `diff`.                                                                                                         |

- `version` is a 14-digit UTC timestamp (`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`). If the clock is not
  past the latest existing version, `diff` uses the second after it, so
  versions only grow.
- `name` must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.
- `.down.sql` files are optional and hand-written (`diff` never generates one).
  They are hashed in `momo.sum`, and `apply` never runs them. Only
  `Engine.Rollback` runs them (section 2).
- Files whose name starts with `.` are ignored everywhere (`.DS_Store`,
  `.momo-*.tmp`). A symlink to a directory inside the migration directory is an
  error. Moving an applied file into a subdirectory is fine: history is keyed by
  version, not path (`TestMovingAppliedMigrationIntoArchiveKeepsHistory`).
- `diff` never overwrites a file (exit 1 if one exists) and writes all-or-none:
  temporaries first, then publish, `momo.sum` last.

### Format versions

| Artifact         | Field                                 | v0.3.0 value | Newer than this binary <!-- x-release-please-version --> |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Snapshot wrapper | `format_version`                      | 1            | read error, "upgrade momo"                               |
| Embedded schema  | `schema.format_version`               | 1            | read error, "upgrade momo"                               |
| `momo.sum`       | header `# momo.sum format=N`          | 1            | read error                                               |
| History table    | `checksum` of the row `__momo_meta__` | 1            | apply refuses, "upgrade momo"                            |

A snapshot without `format_version` is rejected.

### Diff

`momo migrate diff <name>` runs offline (no database, no driver). It loads the
models, compares them with the snapshot of the highest version in the
directory (the empty schema when there is none), orders the changes by
dependency and renders SQL. No difference: prints `no changes`, exit 0, writes
nothing.

- Renames are never guessed. A drop plus an add prints a
  `hint: possible rename ...`; pass `--rename-table old=new` or
  `--rename-column table.old=new`.
- Dropped extensions and schemas are not dropped in the database; `diff` prints
  a hint that they are no longer managed.
- Diff never reads the database. A table that is already populated is
  indistinguishable from an empty one (see section 5).

`diff` does not depend on `momo generate`. `momo generate --check` verifies only
the generated `*_gen.go` files (exit 1 and `stale: <path>` lines when stale).
There is no `momo migrate diff --check`. To fail CI when the models have no
migration, run `momo migrate diff ci_probe` on a clean checkout and fail unless
it prints `no changes` (when there is a difference it writes files and exits 0,
so also check `git status --porcelain` on the migration directory). This recipe
is derived from the code, not covered by a test.

### Checksums

Two independent checks, both SHA-256 of the file bytes:

1. `momo.sum` must match the directory: every file present, none added,
   removed or changed. `Apply`, `Status` and `Baseline` refuse otherwise
   (`ErrChecksumMismatch`, naming the files). A missing `momo.sum` is an error
   that names `momo migrate hash`. `momo.sum` itself carries a directory hash;
   a hand-edited `momo.sum` is rejected.
2. The history row of an applied migration stores the checksum of its up file.
   `Apply` refuses when that file changed since (the error says
   `... changed after version V was applied`).

`Plan` and `Drift` do not check either.

### History table

`momo_migrations`. Every statement against it (read, insert, update, delete
and the `CREATE TABLE`) names the table schema-qualified and quoted, for
example `"app"."momo_migrations"`. The table is resolved before the lock is
taken, and again right after, and the advisory-lock key is built from that
resolved schema, so a migration that changes `search_path` cannot redirect the
history writes. If the two lookups disagree (another process created the table
in an earlier schema in between), the lock is released and the attempt is
repeated once; a second disagreement fails with an error asking you to retry.

- An existing table is found the way earlier versions found it, through the
  session `search_path`, and its schema is then used. Installs made with the
  unqualified name keep working, and no second table is created.
- The resolved object must be a regular, permanent table, and the connecting
  role must be its owner or hold the privileges of the owning role
  (`pg_has_role` with `USAGE`, so a role with NOINHERIT does not qualify). A
  superuser holds every role's privileges, so a superuser migrator
  additionally requires the owner to be itself or another superuser; a table
  owned by an ordinary role is refused, because its triggers and rules would
  run with superuser rights. A view, foreign table, unlogged or temporary table, or a table
  owned by an unrelated role, named `momo_migrations` earlier on the
  `search_path`, is refused with a validation error naming the schema, the
  table and the owner; it is never used. A table adopted on first install by
  `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` passes the same checks after the statement runs.
- What this does and does not defend: it stops a foreign-owned or non-table
  object that sits ahead of the real table on the `search_path` from
  capturing the history writes. It does not stop a role whose privileges you hold,
  or another superuser, from owning such an object, and it cannot protect a schema
  that other roles may write to and that is ahead of yours on the
  `search_path` before any table exists. Keep schemas on the migrator's
  `search_path` writable only by the migrator.
- With no table yet, it is created in the current schema.
  `Config.Schemas[0]` (`migrate.schemas`) must equal the current schema
  (current_schema) or the engine returns a configuration error naming both.
  `plan`, `status` and `drift` on a connection with no current schema and no
  table report an empty history; `apply` and the other writers fail.
- momo does not `SET search_path` for the migration session. Migrations are
  written against the `search_path` of the connection you give momo and may
  rely on it; qualify the history table, not the migrations. Set the
  `search_path` in the connection URL, and pin it per role with
  `ALTER ROLE` on the migrator role.

| Column               | Type             | Meaning                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`            | TEXT PRIMARY KEY | Migration version                                                                         |
| `name`               | TEXT             | Migration name                                                                            |
| `checksum`           | TEXT             | SHA-256 of the up file                                                                    |
| `status`             | TEXT             | `running`, `applied`, `failed`, `rolled_back` (and `meta`)                                |
| `statements_applied` | INTEGER          | Statements that completed                                                                 |
| `error`              | TEXT             | Failure text, empty on success                                                            |
| `applied_at`         | TEXT             | RFC 3339 UTC                                                                              |
| `execution_ms`       | BIGINT           | Duration                                                                                  |
| `apply_id`           | TEXT             | UTC timestamp plus 8 hex digits, shared by one `apply` run; `baseline` for baselined rows |
| `kind`               | TEXT             | `sql`                                                                                     |

One extra row, `version = '__momo_meta__'`, `status = 'meta'`, holds the
history format version. `ReadHistory` and `Inspect` hide it and the table.
`running` and `failed` are "dirty". `rolled_back` is not dirty.

### How apply decides what to run

1. Take the migration lock, set session timeouts, create the history table if
   missing.
2. Refuse (`ErrDirty`, exit 3) if any row is `running` or `failed`.
3. Refuse (`ErrChecksumMismatch`, exit 3) on a checksum problem (above).
4. Pending = every `*.up.sql` and every registered Go migration (section 6a)
   whose version has no row other than
   `rolled_back`, run in ascending version order, optionally stopping after
   `--to N` (a version without a file is refused, so a typo applies nothing).

The test is "has no row", not "is newer than the latest applied". An older file
that appears later (a merged branch) is still applied, after newer ones.
`apply` does not check snapshot parents; `validate` does (section 2).

### Drift

`momo migrate drift` inspects the live database and compares it with the
snapshot of the **latest applied** migration (the empty schema if none, so
every object is unmanaged). Exit 0 and `no drift`, or exit 1 and one line per
finding:

| Line                               | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `changed: <kind> <name>: <detail>` | In both, definition differs. A column, index or constraint present only live is `changed: ... not in snapshot` on that object. An invalid index is `changed: ... invalid index (failed CONCURRENTLY build)`.              |
| `missing: <kind> <name>`           | In the snapshot, not in the database.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `unmanaged: <kind> <name>`         | In the database, not in the snapshot: tables, views, functions, enums, schemas, **extensions** (every extension except `plpgsql`, for example `pg_stat_statements`, `pgcrypto`), and triggers/policies on managed tables. |
| `unverified: <kind> <name>`        | Not compared and does not affect the exit code (below).                                                                                                                                                                   |

- Extension versions are ignored when either side leaves the version empty.
- Hide objects you do not manage with `migrate.exclude` (globs over `name` or
  `schema.name`; they apply to tables, views, functions, enums, extensions,
  triggers and policies). Example: `exclude: ["pg_stat_statements", "audit_*"]`.
- `momo_migrations` is never reported.
- A view query, trigger `WHEN` and policy `USING`/`WITH CHECK` changed outside
  migrations is **not detected**; those objects are listed as `unverified:`
  only. Exit 0 does not prove their text matches. Function bodies are compared.
- Declared text (defaults, checks, index predicates) is canonicalized through a
  scratch schema in a rolled-back transaction, which needs `CREATE` on the
  database. Without it drift still runs but can show false `changed` entries
  (never hides a real one).

## 2. CLI

`momo` has three commands: `generate`, `migrate`, `help`. Global exit codes:
0 success, 1 findings, 2 usage/config, 3 database/lock/execution (migrate).

Shared flags on every `migrate` subcommand: `--config`/`-c momo.yaml`, `--dir`,
`--dialect`, `--url`.

| Command                                                                                                               | Needs DB        | Does                                                                                          | Exit 1 when                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `diff <name> [--rename-table a=b]... [--rename-column t.a=b]... [--allow-destructive] [--stage] [--enforce-not-null]` | no              | Write a migration (section 1, 5).                                                             | destructive or staged refusal; target file exists; model diagnostics                            |
| `plan`                                                                                                                | yes             | List pending migrations with statement counts. Read-only, no lock, creates nothing.           | never                                                                                           |
| `apply [--to N] [--lock-wait 30s]`                                                                                    | yes             | Apply pending.                                                                                | a chain refusal (`ErrBranchConflict`, `ErrChainInvalid`, `ErrOutOfOrder`); other failures are 3 |
| `status`                                                                                                              | yes             | One line per version: `applied`, `pending`, `dirty`, `mismatch`, `missing`. Read-only.        | any version not `applied`/`pending`                                                             |
| `validate [--db]`                                                                                                     | no (`--db` yes) | Directory checks (below); `--db` adds `status`.                                               | any problem or unhealthy status                                                                 |
